#4082. Dune: Awakening's seasonally appropriate Blood and Ice expansion gets a December release date, and in a plus for preservation, an offline mode this month

December is certainly going to be the month of Dune. The biggest Dune of Dunecember will obviously go to Dune: Part 3, which is Duen out December 18th. A little bit before that, however, is a well-timed free expansion coming to Dune: Awakening. It's called Blood and Ice, which sounds gross, but hey, I guess free blood and ice isn't entirely a bad thing?

"The expansion introduces the Polar Sink, an entirely new survival map where everything you've learned about surviving in the desert will be put to the test," explains a Steam blog post. "Instead of protecting yourself from extreme heat, you'll need to find ways to stay warm. The technology you've developed to survive the desert won't be enough here, and you'll need to upgrade your equipment, gather new resources, and adapt your strategies to survive the cold."

You'll find two biomes in the Polar Sink, the tundra and the ice cap, the former being where you'll kick off your time in this expansion. "While conditions here are more manageable than on the ice cap itself, these families won't welcome anyone interfering with their operations," the blog notes. Your main goal is to get the ice cap and gather up all of its valuable resources, namely, ice! Said ice can then be used to "cool your base equipment and speed up production."

Apparently you'll get about 35 more hours of "new progression, along with new vehicle modules, augments, and specialization traits," out of the expansion, and there are plans for future updates that'll give you reason to come back to the Polar Sink in Duen time. Beyond that, there is also a new cosmetic store, which lets you purchase "optional cosmetic items, including outfits, vehicle variants, and additional ways to customize your bases." I'm sure this will go down well.

Perhaps most importantly, this November will see the arrival of offline mode, meaning you don't need an internet connection to play it. Hopefully if (probably when (sorry to be a pessimist (realist))) the servers go down, this means it'll still be playable. Character copying so that you can copy your character from multiplayer servers to single-player will be coming in January, alongside full cross-play. Lots coming essentially!

#4081. Gag Order is a co-op, SCP-ish horror shooter about surviving as best you can against some nasty, tentacle covered cephalopod creatures

Don't let it touch me, please and thank you

What makes Carrion interesting obviously lies in playing as the monster in a horror game rather than being the one chased down by it. The game's nasty tentacle monster still gives me the heebie jeebies, so I really would hate to be hunted by one. This is where I point you towards Gag Order, a shooter where you are in fact hunted by a disgusting cephalopod creature all while tracking down a distress signal.

Gag Order is not designed to be played solo, it feels wrong to call it friendslop given how unfriendly it is in vibes, but it does feel like it fits into a similar lineage as Lethal Company at the very least. In it, you are a research lab's Guardian Unit member, and you get a distress call "from one of the core parts of the complex." Upon arrival, the atmosphere is rotten, and you quickly come to understand that you are not equipped for what you have to deal with.

The solution, then, is to take care of those nightmare-inducing cephalopod creatures. Except during the first phase of a run, it sounds like they're invincible. Your guns do seem to be able to fend them off at the very least, but it's the second phase, which is geared around a "fast paced team-bossight" where it sounds like you'll be trying to take these things down. I'm not quite sure what the process is to get between those two phases, but I'm quite fond of the vibes on display.

It feels a touch reminiscent of 2000s shooters with some slightly contemporary mechanical sensibilities. I'm fond of the light SCP vibes it has going on, alongside the faint surrealness of certain elements like a bunch of crows hanging out in an abandoned office building. Creepy! Good looking stuff. Gag Order is apparently due out by the end of 2026, though we're obviously getting close there, so it's worth keeping an eye on it by throwing it a wishlist on Steam, if it takes your fancy.

#4080. Robert Pattinson rumors heat up as new 007 director says he "can't stop thinking" about Primetime

Is Robert Pattinson the new favorite to play Bond?

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

For weeks, the next James Bond shortlist was narrowed down to four actors: Jack Lowden, Callum Turner, Josh O'Connor – and a mystery name.

In a twist that left most 007 fans shaken and stirred, Robert Pattinson and Nicholas Hoult have reportedly tested (as per Variety) for the role, with many declaring Pattinson – who showcased his spy chops in Tenet – the new frontrunner.

Aiding fuel to the fire is Bond 26 director Denis Villeneuve was asked by Vanity Fair to name a recent movie he can't stop thinking about. Curiously, he answered Primetime, the Robert Pattinson-starring drama where he stars as To Catch a Predator's Chris Hansen.

"I was really impressed by Primetime," Villeneuve said. The director also includes Pattinson as part of his star-studded Dune 3 cast, which perhaps may tip the scales in his favor.

Then there's Nicholas Hoult. A perennial runner-up in big-name auditions (Batman, Superman, and Harry Potter, to name but a few), he is an intriguing new name in the mix for a process that has been played out in public over the past month.

Of the other candidates, Jack Lowden has broken his silence on being linked as a prospective new Bond actor, but with the sort of subtlety that might see him welcomed into the corridors of MI6.

Lowden told British GQ, "On this… It’s all very flattering. It’s nice to be mentioned – for any role – and I’m just not really going to add to the noise."

For more on 007's past missions, we have our ranking of the best James Bond movies.

#4078. Talking Point: What Made The Xbox 360 Era So Incredible In Your Opinion?

As we continue celebrating the past 25 years of Xbox throughout the course of the month, we thought we'd use this opportunity to look at the Xbox 360 - a console that's consistently rated as the best system in the history of the brand.

The Xbox 360 will be turning 21 years old on November 22nd, and its impact is still being felt today. This is the console that gave us such features as Party Chat, modern-style Xbox dashboards, the ability to download mainstream games digitally, and a ridiculous number of incredible franchises that have won over the hearts and minds of many.

For what it's worth, we did actually talk about some of this stuff for the 20th anniversary last year:

Feature Seven Things We Miss About The Xbox 360 Era In 2025

As we rapidly approach its 20th anniversary

With that said though, every era of Xbox has treated us to innovative new features and amazing games that have stood the test of time. The PS3 existed at the same time as the Xbox 360, and yet somehow, Microsoft's console felt like the more popular of the two, despite selling slightly less units overall in the end.

It even managed to navigate a devastating technical issue in the form of the Red Ring of Death, and somehow still convince the masses that it was one of the greatest consoles of all time. That's some feat.

So, what made the Xbox 360 era so incredible in your opinion? Was it just a brilliantly-designed system, RROD aside? Did it innovate in ways that no other system did? Were the games simply that good? Or has its popularity become overblown since the horribly botched launch of the Xbox One in 2013?

Let us know your thoughts on why the Xbox 360 era was so good down in the comments section below.

Exclusive Xbox 360 Fan Talks To Us About Completing Their Collection After 20 Years

"My mission is to get achievements in every single game..."

Fraser is the News Editor at Pure Xbox, where he spends his time reporting on the biggest stories in the world of Xbox and beyond.

It had all the best titles, plenty of exclusives and the broadest content. It was an exciting platform

What made it special was creative games, exclusives and visual gap: innovative titles for their time, featuring beautiful HD 3D graphics and smooth gameplay. It was also the era of creative games and iconic franchises like Gears of War, Mass Effect, Dead Space, and BioShock.

I feel like this is the formula that Asha is trying to recreate with Helix: a return to exclusive games and a revolutionary technical platform. What's still missing is the creativity aspect, and that's where I still have some doubts, just as I do about the industry as a whole. Risk-taking has become minimal, and we're being flooded with remasters and sequels.

That said, considering the enormous cost of game development today, I can understand why risks have to be carefully calculated. Even so, Xbox has been by far the most creative platform of this console generation compared to its competitors, so hopefully that continues.

Exclusives, ambition and superior versions.

Pixel shaders. A lot of people don’t even know what they are, but they are the reason the visual quality jump from the previous generation to that one was so huge and why we have not seen anything like it since. We have seen a slow gradual fidelity increase, but it’s likely we won’t ever again see such a generational leap in a single day.

Streamlined online okay was also huge. Even to this day, with the amazing advancements in Steam APIs, nothing comes close in PCs to the streamlined nature of the console ecosystem matchmaking that was introduced that generation. PC gamers still to this day rely on multiple apps.

The introduction of achievements was also huge. Ignoring the OCD obsession to 100% a title, having these “digital footprints” made gaming experiences feel a lot more… social, even in single player games.

It also was the first console to open itself to indie developers, even if still drastically restricted for today’s standards. The impact this had on mainstream gaming should never be understated.

The technology and the games it made possible. Both PC and consoles were pushing the rendering tech forward. People were anxious to get their hands on the next jump in gaming tech (and phone and TV).

Red Dead, sneakily playing Godfather 2 because of the club where you could see the topless ladies. Obviously the 360 had great games, and typically the best versions of cross-platform games (excluding PC of course), all with achievements and no forced installs. The online store got 2-3 new XBLA games every week, all with demos that unlocked via unlock keys, so if you liked the game you could buy it and not have to re-download it.

The first couple of hardware revisions were noisy/rattly and failure-prone, but everything else was so good that people put up with it. It's a shame the launch model wasn't like the 360 S or 360 E, cos then it would be hard to criticise it at all.

The Xbox 360 is simply one of the best and most influential consoles of all time. As time has gone by, its legacy and influence has grown exponentially. It was the first to have a storefront on console. It lead the way in championing indie games and making the transition to digital consumption. Achievements spawned trophies on PlayStation. Party chat, another key feature first on Xbox 360, would arrive on PlayStation an entire generation later (Nintendo only recently adopted it lol). Then you have the games; so many of them great and diverse. Single player, multiplayer and co-op were all covered on 360. People talk about PS4 being the true successor to PS2 (to skip over the disappointment of PS3) but in all honesty it was the true successor to the Xbox 360. It did what the 360 did but better and more improved. I recall Microsoft bundling early 360 models with a free headset. Sony did likewise on PS4 (remember the one ear piece?). Even competitors took notes from it. That is the legacy of the Xbox 360.

There’s more I can say about the 360 particularly regarding where Microsoft got it wrong and how that lead to their current situation but that’s for another time.

We started to see fewer original IP, visuals homogenized into the piss filter that the generation became famously known for, and there were fewer and fewer risks with every game. The Xbox 360 featured an exclusive title called Lost Odyssey, arguably the greatest JRPG ever created. While most JRPGs are aimed at a younger audience and tend to feature straightforward, simple narratives, Lost Odyssey takes a different approach. Its core, titled "A Thousand Years of Dreams, A Thousand Years of Memories"—which explores the protagonist’s past—was penned by Kiyoshi Shigematsu, a recipient of the prestigious Naoki Prize. These stories delve into universal themes: the experience of loss and separation, a profound sense of emptiness, and the sorrow of having neither a place to return to nor a destination to head toward. Much of this content is written with those in the twilight of their lives in mind.The main storyline is also rooted in the personal tragedies experienced by the project’s executive producer, Hironobu Sakaguchi.The game boasts a top-tier creative team, including character designs by Takehiko Inoue (Slam Dunk, Vagabond) and a musical score by Nobuo Uematsu—some of the finest talent to ever work on an Xbox title.Even today, many fans continue to hope for a remake or a sequel.

#4077. Delightful Tidying Up Indie Gets A Surprise Switch 2 Edition Today, Complete With 120fps

Admirers of 2022's delightful little 'tidy 'em up', A Little To The Left, will want to pay attention to this one. Developer Max Inferno and publisher Secret Mode have announced the game's Switch 2 Edition, and it's available today!

Launching to celebrate the game's fourth anniversary, A Little to the Left - Nintendo Switch 2 Edition boasts a smooth 120fps, Mouse Mode controls, faster load times, a visual boost, and USB mouse and keyboard support.

The best part is that the upgrade path is completely free for all those who own the base game on Switch 1. The NS2E store page isn't live at the time of writing, but considering that the original only set us back £12.99 / $14.99, we can't imagine this new version will be particularly bank-breaking.

Max Inferno also has a patch inbound for all versions of the game, which targets a few known issues in the Daily Tidy mode and Seeing Stars DLC puzzles.

The fiddly controls were one of our biggest hangups with the original release on Switch 1, which we otherwise said "provides an experience that is a weird mingling of the semi-passive and viscerally intrusive" in our 8/10 review. Let's hope that everything plays as it should in this new version.

#4076. As if the injury descriptions weren't already ghastly enough in Dwarf Fortress, the legendary outpost builder is getting a "meat biome"

"Lots of meat terrain - muscle, bone, vertebral walls, sinew, sphincters."

Legendary outpost builder Dwarf Fortress is getting a meat biome. A terrible netherworld of bone and artery. A sunken redoubt of gristle and gizzard. An appalling labyrinth of squirt and squelch. Honestly, the biggest shock here is that Dwarf Fortress doesn't appear to have a meat biome already. It certainly has plenty of florid descriptions of fatal injuries.

These foul omens arrive care of a massive "Future of the Fortress" thread on the Bay 12 forums, in which studio co-founder (and prominent genAI disliker) Tarn "Toady One" Adams fields questions about the on-going development. As a forum thread, it's not a formal news source, so please season these tales of gutsy geology with whatever Condiment of Scepticism you consider appropriate.

There's no date for when the new biome might arrive, but Adams says it'll likely exist underground, and will be revolting. "Lots of meat terrain - muscle, bone, vertebral walls, sinew, sphincters," he promised. "We would have rivers of blood/fluids if we ever get to the fluid update, but no new fluids as it stands. We had thrown out the idea for maple syrup style taps on the vertebral walls for cosmic spinal fluid but alas, this is not in the game." At the very least, there won't be any meat trees, but you can mine the meat for resources.

Adams doesn't discuss the origins of the meat biome in the thread – is it more of a headless, fungal phenomenon, or is there some kind of huge mammalian cadaver down there? If it's the latter, one consolation is that the meat biome can't be resurrected. "Ha ha, I don't think regular meat can be animated currently?" Adams remarked in response to a question about biomes of squirming, zombified meat. "So probably not."

The bulk of the conversation around Dwarf Fortress at present concerns forthcoming changes to the magic system, together with how arcane knowledge is categorised, transmitted, preserved and lost throughout each procedurally generated world. There's a lot of speculative chat about that in the Future of the Fortress thread, too much to cleanly summarise. It's saying something about the density and stature of Dwarf Fortress that the addition of flesh caves feels like an afterthought.

Developer Bay 12's current plans for the game also include a crystal biome, which I would say is the nicer option, but then I remembered that this is Dwarf Fortress, the game in which you might end up getting besieged by the ghosts of the very children you callously sent to hunt down a wild elephant. There is absolutely going to be something in the crystal biome that gives you nightmares. Dazzling, prismatic nightmares.

Stranger Things fans think that a Christmas special is on the way

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Over 10 months after Stranger Things season 5 ended, it seems that the secret episode theories just won't die. Following the excitement of Stranger Things Day 2026, fans now believe that there is a Christmas special on the way.

If you're thinking, 'wait, hasn't this been going on ever since the show came to a close?' Yes, you're right. But new evidence has fans theorising that the secret episode they had been holding out for may end up being something more festive after finding that some set photos from the final season don't quite add up.

In multiple images, posted by one fan on Twitter, we can see Christmas decorations dotted around Hawkins, as well as a personalised bauble reading 'The Wheelers 1989 .' This doesn't really make sense, as season 5 was set in November 1989, with no mention of Christmas. However, this could just be extra set pieces from filming, but it sure does add fuel to the already wild secret episode theory.

#lovewinsgate #conformitygate #btsgate the reason why we can assume that we’ll get at least some volume for xmas btw https://t.co/7KPX77JVFDNovember 8, 2026

In case you're new here, let me give you a rundown on the situation. When the sci-fi series came to a close on New Year's Day, some fans were so disappointed that they refused to accept the ending. Fans picked out mistakes and 'clues' that looked to suggest that the finale was just a ruse set up by Vecna, theorizing that a secret ninth episode was on January 7. This was known as Conformity Gate. But, of course, the alternate ending never arrived, seemingly bringing Conformity Gate to an end.

However, Stranger Things Day 2026, the annual holiday that takes place on November 6, marking the disappearance of Will Byers, has set the theory alive again. Fans spotted clues that big news was on the way, from secret messages posted by The Weather Channel and The Wheel of Fortune to a cryptic Instagram story from the show's co-creator Ross Duffer. This turned out to be in relation to an upcoming 2028 prequel series titled 'Other Worlds: A Stranger Things Adventure,' which Netflix announced with a short teaser.

For now, Netflix hasn't given any indication that any further Stranger Things episodes are on the bar, bar the upcoming prequel and Stranger Things: Tales from '85 season 2. But fans continue to hold out hope.

Stranger Things is available to watch in its entirety on Netflix. For more, check out our guide to the best Netflix shows, and keep up with new shows on the way.

#4073. Skyblivion modders reveal a former volunteer is "threatening to sue for damages upwards of €30,000" over work on the unofficial Oblivion remake project

"I just hope that we can get this resolved as soon as possible and get on with the planned release"

The team behind Oblivion remake mod Skyblivion are being threatened with legal action by a former volunteer on the project, according a video posted by current lead Kyle 'Rebelzize' Rebel. The situation looks like it'll need resolving before the mod, which was originally set to release last year, can finally make its way out of the Imperial City sewers.

"Recently, a former volunteer who contributed to Skyblivion’s development departed the project," the Skyblivion team outlined in a written statement and a YouTube video presented by Rebel. "We want to be completely transparent with the community about what has happened since their departure. After they left the project, we had several discussions regarding the continued use and maintenance of his work. The main disagreement centered on their objection to our decompilation of parts of their work — a necessary step our team took to maintain functionality and fix issues in systems already built into the project after access to the original source code repository was revoked."

"To protect ourselves from more stress and try and ensure a clean break, we decided to take the high road," Rebel explained in the video. "We have removed that work entirely. Thankfully due to some of our volunteers stepping up and simply learning new skill sets, as well as help from prominent Skyrim modders and permissions to use and integrate existing Skyrim mods, we've been able to implement replacements that we think fit Skyblivion's needs, in some cases even better than what we had before."

However, Rebel and co claim that despite them making it "clear multiple times to this former volunteer that we have removed their contributions", the ex-Skyblivion dev is "threatening to sue for damages upwards of €30,000". They claim that the ex-volunteer's legal threats "demand personal information of multiple volunteers [on Skyblivion] including full names and addresses". Rebel noted that the team see these demands as "something that we are simply not willing to share with someone that we don't even know" and feel are "just completely disproportionate for what's really going on".

The modders say they've consulted with legal counsel already and have a lawyer on standby if necessary. Though, since said lawyer's services will - the Skyblivion team claim - cost €2,500, they've put out a call for anyone with "a background in IP law or GDPR law" willing to offer them pro bono legal aid to get in touch via the mod's website.

"Please don't turn this into any kind of witch hunt, despite this very unfortunate situation," Rebel said in closing. "We don't wish ill on a former volunteer over all this and I just hope that we can get this resolved as soon as possible and get on with the planned release, which is really what we're working towards. You will hear more from us soon on the actual release."

This situation makes it two years running that Skyblivion's found itself engulfed in drama during the final months of what's supposed to be its release year. In 2025, former volunteer Dee Keyes had a public disagreement with the project's leads over whether releasing the mod that year was a reasonable or achievable goal. Skyblivion was subsequently delayed into 2026.

This past weekend, Keyes tweeted a response to the Skyblivion team's statement on the alleged legal threats. "I've had my issues with the project and left because of it, but I left knowing that my work would remain with [Skyblivion] (happily so) and didn't want to hurt the project's progress," he wrote. "I understand [the former volunteer] being upset, but I really don't see why they'd go so far as to demand their work ripped out."

Here's hoping the Skyblivion team and the ex-volunteer can resolve things without all the expense and effort that'd inevitably be necessary if the dispute ends up in court. Given there are now less than two months left of 2026, and Skyblivion's modders have this on their plates on top of any remaining work needed to finish their creation, I'd personally be very surprised if its release doesn't end up being pushed into next year.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

It was only a matter of (very short) time before Ocarina of Time remake exploits would come to light following Nintendo's big launch of the revamped Legend of Zelda entry last week – and, well, it only took days.

The original Ocarina of Time from 1998 boasts a plethora of fan-led glitches and "hacks," so to speak, for speedrunning and the like – and the remake offers no exception. While some of the old methods have changed, such as those reliant on the auto-jump system, folks are now unearthing new exploits, including a couple that let Link jump infinitely… even into areas he's not supposed to be in as a child, pre-Temple of Time travel.

If you've not seen it yourself, there are two versions circulating the web: one that involves cycling through your quick menu between two items, as posted over on X, and another known as "actor jumping," which is arguably too broken.

Encontraram um bug em Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake que permite ao Link realizar pulos infinitos. Graças a esse glitch, é possível alcançar o topo de Hyrule Castle controlando o Link criança. https://t.co/MdGKcVdzRgNovember 8, 2026

You can learn more about it on YouTube, but put simply, it's got fans accessing areas they're not meant to be in as child Link, leading to some, erm, head-scratching textures.

A quick video of how Link looks following this exploit says it all, showing a stretched-out (cursed) iteration of Hyrule's little hero – and yes, the comments deliver.

We can now beat Shadow Temple as child, which automatically turns you into adult. We still have 1 roadblock to get past before this can be used in a speedrun, but it'll be huge assuming we can get past it. It also looks very funny. https://t.co/s2aoTKCQyYNovember 8, 2026

"We got Lonk and Lunk," reads one, screenshots of the horrifying stretchy Link attached. Others see more fans post their own images of the creepy visual effect, with Link sometimes appearing genuinely more fearsome than a Dead Hand.

Another thread shows the lanky Link entering the Bongo Bongo boss arena in the Shadow Temple, and it's as hilarious as it is terrifying.

#4071. "Mario Is My Life" - Beloved Blogger 'Supper Mario Broth' Reveals Health Issues

"Only blindness or death will result in me no longer posting Mario facts"

The author of the beloved Mario-related blog Supper Mario Broth has posted a health update revealing he has heart failure.

This comes via a social post in which he states he has "a 2/3 chance of surviving past one year with this condition." Despite "a lifelong commitment to a healthy lifestyle", he says his decline in health is due to underlying genetic causes.

A complication from his diagnosis is retinopathy, which is essentially the degradation of the retina that can result in a loss of sight and may affect his ability to research Mario games, post facts, and run the blog in the future.

I am scared I will soon not be able to see Mario again. However, I promise that until that day arrives, I will always be here, posting Mario facts. Thank you all so much for your support through the years.

Despite this news, he has stressed an ongoing commitment to Supper Mario Broth, stating that "only blindness or death will result in me no longer posting Mario facts." He goes on to say that the announcement is not a request for help before thanking readers for all their support over the years.

His posts have been inundated with support. User 'rainbow batsuit' says, "Even if you never post a single fact again, the legacy of joy and discovery you have already built will live on in our hearts for untold years." All of us here at Nintendo Life wholeheartedly agree.

The blog's latest post relating to Mario reveals that it's actually possible to use Dry Bones in Super Mario Maker 2 to play the ocarina in Zelda: Ocarina of Time on Switch 2 via the console's built-in mic.

In The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for Nintendo Switch 2, it is possible to play the ocarina using Dry Bones in Super Mario Maker 2.

We're sure the entire Nintendo Life community will join us in sending Broth our thanks and very best wishes.

Nintendo Life’s resident horror fanatic, when he’s not knee-deep in Resident Evil and Silent Hill lore, Ollie likes to dive into a good horror book while nursing a lovely cup of tea. He also enjoys long walks and listens to everything from TOOL to Chuck Berry.

This dude does not deserve the (now literal) heartache he's been subjected to over the last few years, he's one of the most genuine people I've seen on the internet. Hope he retains the ability to continue sharing his passions for many years to come!

Never heard of this person or website, but man, that is such a sad story. I'm very sorry for their condition and prognosis and wish them at least a smooth and relatively painless future.

Man, between this and the untimely death of the Saga series localization director... Just makes you realize how tragically brief life can be, no matter what you do to help yourself. Thankfully both these individuals have left a legacy and touched people's lives in ways we should all aspire to. I sincerely hope the person behind Supper Mario Broth survives this ordeal.

Supper Mario Broth is one of the shining lights of social media and the video game enthusiast space - his posts always bring a smile to my face. I'm praying for as smooth a journey as possible in the days ahead.

Hate to hear it first and foremost for him, but even more so since I quite enjoyed Supper Mario Broth (didn't check it out regularly, but whenever I did it was great) - absolutely sending my thanks and best wishes, too!

As others have said, he's one of the most positive voices in the Nintendo online space. He makes me feel like a fake Mario fan because he's always sharing obscure trivia I had no idea about. His posts are always incredibly fascinating, though, and he runs his account with such professionalism that he should be getting paid as a social media manager.

Oh no! That is very sad. I know next to nothing of his personal life, but seems a real good dude. I love his love for Mario. That alone makes me happy. His posts on Twitter are always a good read. I shall pray that he is ok and can be as happy and healthy as long as possible.

What an icon. It's never the Putins or Kims of the world, just the ones who actually make the world just a little bit brighter. Such sad news. My prayers will be with him.

Reading this was genuinely heartrending. Praying fervently for the best outcome

Man, this ruined my day. I love his posts and check the blog fairly often. Hoping for the best.

Could Lando Calrissian return in Ahsoka season 2?

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Ahsoka season 2 has added Death Stranding star Tommie Earl Jenkins to the cast as a still-unknown character. But Star Wars fans have put two and two together and come up with a theory we can get behind: what if Jenkins is playing Lando Calrissian?

Reports of Jenkins' casting in Ahsoka season 2 emerged in April 2026 when Star Wars sleuths noticed Ahsoka season 2 on Jenkins' Actors Access page. While never officially confirmed by Disney, we now know that Jenkins will appear in season 2 as Sabine Wren star Natasha Liu Bordizzo posted that Jenkins' scenes in the new season "made her cry" in a response on Instagram. And it's this emotional reaction that has put the Lando theory machine into overdrive.

The theory, posted by moraithemessenger on X, is supported by a few pieces of circumstantial evidence. First, Jenkins must be playing a significant character if his scenes were enough to make his co-star Bordizzo cry, not simply some random Rebel commander. Second, Jenkins reportedly filmed scenes with Eman Esfandi's Ezra Bridger. And perhaps most importantly, Lando already crossed paths with the Rebels crew in the season one episode, 'Idiot's Array'.

Recently, Esfandi revealed on stage at LA Comic Con that "other well-beloved characters" from Rebels and/or The Clone Wars will appear in live-action in Ahsoka season 2, and that "everyone's going to be really happy with them." Jenkins playing Lando would certainly make anyone who saw his scene-stealing performance as Die-Hardman in Death Stranding happy.

As some have pointed out, at 60 years old, Jenkins is a little older than Lando would be at this point in the Star Wars timeline (where he'd be about 50), but we know that Lando is still kicking around the Galaxy at this time, as he survives up to the events of The Rise of Skywalker. And given that Luke Skywalker popped up in The Mandalorian season 2 finale and The Book of Boba Fett, bringing back beloved original trilogy characters for streaming shows like Ahsoka is not off the table.

Even if the Lando theories are wide of the mark, we at least know that Ahsoka season 2 is set to feature more Clone Wars flashbacks. Anakin Skywalker star Hayden Christensen even wants to get the band back together and make a live-action Clone Wars show.

Ahsoka season 2 streams on Disney Plus from January 20, 2027. While we wait, check out our guide on all the other upcoming Star Wars movies and shows.

#4069. 10+ Game Pass Titles Are Confirmed For Xbox's 25th Anniversary Week

We're heading into Xbox's 25th anniversary week! Xbox will officially be celebrating that milestone on Sunday, November 15th (exactly seven days from the time of posting this article), and we're hoping for some surprises along the way.

We already know of one surprise, which is that eight games will be joining Xbox Game Pass Essential on the 15th itself. Combine that with the six others during the rest of the week, and we've got over 10 brand-new additions heading to Game Pass during the course of the 25th anniversary period.

In case you missed them, those eight Game Pass Essential games on the 15th are as follows:

As for the rest, we've got three games arriving on the 10th, two arriving on the 11th, and one on the 12th. There's every chance Microsoft might add to these as we go, but these are the ones that have been confirmed so far.

A highlight for many will be John Carpenter's Toxic Commando on November 12th, which is an awesome take on the classic Left 4 Dead formula, while all the others are "day one" launches, including the extremely addictive Football Manager 27, the Vampire Survivors-like Warhammer Survivors, and BMX postman game Tanuki: Pon's Summer.

Instead of just throwing these ones into a table, we're going to leave them down below with trailers and descriptions, and we'll be sure to remind you on the relevant dates when they become available with your Game Pass subscription.

On this page: 10+ Game Pass Titles Are Confirmed For Xbox's 25th Anniversary Week

Choose the club. Shape the squad. Set the tactics. Chase the future only you can see. FM27 is where your footballing beliefs become a reality. Make The Call.

The Tanuki Festival is just a month away, and the shrine is in disrepair. Follow Pon, a well meaning, if a bit lazy Tanuki with a part-time job at the Post Office, as he works to restore the shrine before summer ends. Deliver packages, make friends, and get the shrine ready for the big festival!

Warhammer Survivors is the official grim and dark bullet-heaven game from the developers of Warhammer 40,000 Boltgun. Play as over 40 iconic champions from the Warhammer 40,000 and Warhammer Age of Sigmar universes and obliterate those who champion death and destruction.

17-year-old Hope Song thought the national exams were her biggest worry... until she got home to a ransacked apartment and two missing parents. Investigate through the eyes of an artist, turn sketches into evidence, and watch her family's mystery grow stranger and darker with every answer.

Thronefall is a minimalist strategy game where you build a humble kingdom by day and defend it by night. Balance economy and defense by fortifying walls, recruiting troops, and charging into battle yourself to protect your stronghold from relentless waves of attackers.

Pick a character and team up with three friends ‘cause it’s time to save the world. Experience intense FPS action as you obliterate hordes of terrifying monsters! You may not be on the best team of mercenaries, but you are… a Toxic Commando!

#4068. New PS Portal Announced, Future-Proofed with Internal Storage and Only for Japan

New version in black is exclusive to Japan

Sony has today announced a new model of the PS Portal will be future-proofed with the addition of internal storage. The new version is launching on 10th December 2026 at the same price as the current model (¥39,980), but only in Japan.

Just like the Japan-specific PS5 console Sony sells, this new PS Portal model can only be set to the Japanese language and use a PSN account from the Japan region.

The new model also comes in black, but the big detail here is the fact Sony has "an eye towards future functionality", as it includes internal storage for the PS Portal. More information on that front is coming soon.

It doesn't share any further details on what the addition might entail, but the PS6 is rumoured to have a handheld device supporting the home console. Might that have something to do with the PS Portal refresh? This model also comes with a month of PS Plus Premium bundled in, so you can start streaming PS5 games straight away.

Since you don't need a PS5 anymore to stream your games, and can just do it via a PS Plus Premium membership, Sony is also updating this new model's name:

"Reflecting this expansion of gameplay beyond remote play, the product name for this new model has been changed from 'PlayStation Portal Remote Player' to 'PlayStation Portal Player.'"

The new PS Portal mode is available to pre-order from 13th November 2026, with a view to releasing on 10th December in Japan. We'll keep you updated on whether this updated version is announced for other territories.

#4067. Delve into "a deep underground facility full of secrets and horrors" in the latest Fallout 4 quest mod from the Commonwealth Story Expansion Project

A mysterious bunker with out of this world contents

After adding a whole new town to Fallout 4 last month, a group of modders have released another in their long string of extra quests for the RPG. This latest mission revolves around a dungeon delve in the Glowing Sea, where a mysterious bunker's just been unearthed.

"The harsh radioactive winds of the Glowing Sea have uncovered a deep underground facility full of secrets and horrors," the group behind the Commonwealth Story Expansion Project (CSEP) declared the description of this latest work, Under The Stars.

A fresh dungeon with a quest attached, the mod tasks you with donning your hazmat suit for a trip to a sunken bunker in the region of post-apocalyptic Boston with the least chill weather. Inside await voiced holotapes and puzzles offering clues as to what went down in this cosy corner of the Commonwealth, plus some new gear to make braving whatever lurks within worth it.

Spoilers: Judging by the screenshots, it looks like the place is an Area 51-esque hidey-hole for evidence of aliens and other cryptic oddities.

If you're unfamiliar, the CSEP lot are responsible for a bunch of popular Fallout 4 quest mods based around the likes of deadly cults, underground wars, post-apocalyptic detective work, and Brotherhood of Steel drama. While Under The Stars doesn't look have been as big an undertaking as those, that previous form points to it being an expertly-crafted addition that'll slot seamlessly into the game.

The modders have put Under The Stars together as part of a community-hosted modding jam called Fallout Flood, with this latest one based around the theme of being underground. Among the other works to have come out of it thus far are another Fallout 4 quest mod dubbed Stranded - The Oasis, a dungeon full of funky rats called the S'Laven, and a new robot enemy you can wear as a hat. It's also produced a New Vegas quest mod about exploring an abandoned NCR railway, so seems to have been very productive gathering of modding minds.

To give Under The Stars a go, your copy of Fallout 4 will need to have the Automatron and Vault-Tec Workshop DLCs.

Adam Driver explains why he finally said yes to Marvel

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Adam Driver might have repeatedly turned down Marvel before, but he finally said yes to playing Mr. Sinister in the upcoming X-Men movie.

Speaking on Jimmy Kimmel Live, Driver revealed why he decided this was the right project to join the MCU.

"I was a big X-Men fan when I was a kid," Driver said, and, when Kimmel asked if that meant the comics, he agreed and added "and the TV show," which was "right in my generation."

"I was a big fan. I mean, I was a fan of the other things too, but this one felt like a right time, and then it's X-Men," Driver shared.

He added: "It was really X-Men and Jake Schreier, who's the director, his idea for it, and that it's Kevin Feige. It all kind of came together. The script is really cool."

When Kimmel suggested Driver was being "careful" by checking the project out beforehand, Driver also made sure to say, "A lot of people are going to watch it, and, if it's bad, a lot of people will see you being bad. Plus, I don't want to mess it up. I'm a huge fan of X-Men." Check out the moment below.

adam talking about joining the mcu he grew up seeing the tv show & playing wolverine with his cousin. he has read a script of the new x-men film https://t.co/9KCHM0S8qzNovember 6, 2026

Driver's enthusiasm is certainly a reason to get excited – and the rest of the cast is pretty stacked, too. The new X-Men line-up features Kit Connor as Cyclops, Christopher Abbott as Professor X, Inde Navarette as Rogue, Maya Boyd as Storm, and Samara Weaving as Emma Frost, as revealed at this year's D23.

Before then, though, we'll see the Fox-era X-Men back for one last rodeo in December's Avengers: Doomsday. The returning cast members include Ian McKellen's Magneto, Alan Cumming's Nightcrawler, Rebecca Romijn's Mystique, James Marsden's Cyclops, and the late Patrick Stewart's Professor X.

Channing Tatum will also be back as Gambit, after debuting in Deadpool and Wolverine. He recently revealed his character is from the same Marvel timeline as the other X-Men, but "with gray around it."

Doomsday arrives this December 18, while the new X-Men film is slated for release on May 5, 2028. While you wait, check out our guide to all the most exciting upcoming Marvel movies and TV shows for everything else that's in store.

#4065. Feature: Five Reasons Why 2026 Is The Best Time Ever To Be An Xbox Series X|S Owner

The two consoles are celebrating their sixth anniversary on November 10th

We've got a lot of anniversaries taking place over the next few weeks, including the big 25th anniversary of Xbox on November 15th, but we thought we'd first take a moment to celebrate the Xbox Series X|S anniversary as well.

Both of these consoles launched six years ago on November 10th of 2020, and Pure Xbox was there at the time with a big celebration of the launch along with an unboxing preview, a full review, and various bits of coverage.

Hardware Review Xbox Series X - The Fastest, Most Powerful Xbox Ever

A lot has changed over this past six years for Xbox (and indeed, the gaming industry at large), and not all of it has been for the better by any means. As someone who picked up an Xbox Series X at launch though, I reckon 2026 has been the best time ever to own the console, so this seems like a good chance to highlight some reasons why!

Here are those five reasons — in my personal opinion — on why it's so good to own an Xbox Series console right now:

Prior to this year, there had been a lot of disgruntlement amongst the fanbase over the "This is an Xbox" marketing campaign that essentially told us the Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S weren't all that important anymore. That might not have been the intention, but it's certainly the impression that many fans came away with.

We've seen a complete change in 2026 though, with Asha Sharma's new leadership team insisting that console is a major focus for them, and implementing an absolute ton of new console-specific features throughout the year. From Mythic Achievements to new startup animations, it's been an amazing year for console updates without a doubt.

The obvious benefit to being an Xbox Series X|S owner this late in the lifecycle is that you get access to a tonne of great games from over the years. 2026 has been an incredible year for new releases too — both first-party and third-party — and I think Xbox Game Pass also enjoyed another really fruitful year complete with many "day one" releases.

My personal backlog is extensive at this point, and it doesn't help that ID@Xbox keeps knocking it out of the park with so many great indie releases on a monthly basis. Xbox Play Anywhere is growing on an extremely impressive scale as well, meaning I can play loads of my purchased Series X|S games on PC whenever I want to.

Despite what some might think, we've had exclusives on Xbox consoles over the past six years, but most of them have been of the third-party variety. Gears of War: E-Day changed all that in October when it become the first permanent console exclusive that Xbox has published in a long time, and it'll be followed up by Clockwork Revolution in 2027.

In other words, you're going to need an Xbox Series X, an Xbox Series S or a powerful enough PC to play these games going forward, which certainly makes these consoles more attractive for fans of certain titles and franchises. I'm certainly comforted knowing that I already own a Series X for when Xbox decides to make even more games exclusive.

Grand Theft Auto 6 is going to have the biggest video game launch of all time, and that's only going to happen across PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. There's no PC version whatsoever right now, and fans could be waiting until well into next year until they get a native Windows release of the game.

That automatically makes it a fantastic time to be an Xbox Series X|S owner if you're interested in GTA 6! All of the pre-release footage has been on base PS5, which means it should look basically the same on the Xbox Series X. Everyone's a little bit more concerned about the Series S version, but this is Rockstar we're talking about - they're surely going to pull out all the stops to optimise the biggest game ever for Microsoft's lower-powered console.

It's not usually the case that we're talking about a strong future for six-year-old consoles, but the video game industry isn't in a normal place right now. Everyone knows about the component crisis that's causing prices to vastly increase across the board - something that's affected new purchases of the Series X and S as well.

However, with rumours that Xbox's Project Helix console (potentially set for 2028) could cost well over $1,000, it seems more likely than ever that the Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S have still got long futures ahead of them. Combine that with all the new console features that have been added this year, plus the arrival of new technology such as AMD FSR Upscaling 4.1, and it looks like there's a lot more life left in these consoles going forward.

Again, I appreciate that it's not a great time to buy an Xbox Series X or Series S right now due to the aforementioned component crisis, and here's hoping we might at least get some Black Friday deals in a few weeks' time.

For the rest of us who already own one though, this has got to be the best time ever, right? Amazing games, loads of new features, exclusives, GTA 6... I'm very glad to own an Xbox Series X sitting here in November of 2026.

My only fear? That it'll suddenly break and I'll have spend an absolute fortune on a new one.

Could GTA 6 Online be arriving sooner than expected?

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

GTA 6's launch is right around the corner, and according to a PlayStation Store sleuth who almost got the game's monstrous file size totally correct weeks ago, there are already hints of GTA Online's existence – even though Rockstar Games continues to remain tight-lipped on that.

Per PlayStation Game Size on Twitter – best known for posting information about the download sizes of PlayStation games ahead of their launch – a handful of clues have reportedly been uncovered suggesting that GTA Online compatibility is already somewhat present in the game, even if its actual multiplayer component hasn't been added. Supposedly, these are: 'intentType": "joinSession"', 'intentType": "launchActivity"', and 'intentType": "launchMultiplayerActivity"'.

GTA 6 has been billed as a single-player experience, so what reason would there be for an option to join sessions or multiplayer activities if something like GTA Online wasn't being added?

Grand Theft Auto VI supports : intentType": "joinSession" intentType": "launchActivity" intentType": "launchMultiplayerActivity"November 9, 2026

Of course, the assumption amongst fans has been that GTA 6 Online is inevitable – the current version of GTA Online continues to be an enormous breadwinner for Rockstar over 13 years since its launch, so it'd be in the devs' interest to keep the ball rolling there. Beyond that, court documents from the start of the year made reference to now-former devs discussing a "difficult" 32-player session, which would match up with how many players you can fit in a GTA 5 Online session, too.

In terms of this latest 'evidence,' it's wise to take it with a pinch of salt, though PlayStation Game Size does tend to be relatively reliable. A couple of weeks ago, they claimed that GTA 6 would have a 210GB download size, though Rockstar later announced it was a 212GB pre-load. To be fair to them, it wouldn't be unusual to see some fluctuation here if Rockstar had queued up any updates or fixes in the time since their initial post.

So much so, in fact, that in their latest series of posts today, PlayStation Game Size also claimed that the size for the worldwide version of GTA 6 has gone up to 223.088GB. They specified "worldwide" because, oddly, the version releasing in New Zealand and Australia was apparently showing as 0.008GB smaller – though they noted that "the package size can be different from the download size." In their most recent post, the Australian pre-load is shown as being 209.913GB, proving their point.

Regardless, though, fans are excited – many are now hoping that Online could be arriving sooner than previously anticipated if some of the infrastructure is seemingly already in place. "They're going to shadowdrop Online in December aren't they," one speculates. "Online is probably March I'd say," guesses another. "GTA6 online on day 1," another proclaims. There's, uh, not a lot of consistency in folks' theories.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

Anyway, we'll just have to stay tuned to see what ends up being accurate – or not. Even though Rockstar hasn't officially announced GTA 6 Online, it does feel like the kind of thing that'd be just a matter of time.

Rockstar could release GTA 6 on PC sooner to head off AI ports, former Grand Theft Auto lead suggests: "I think I would be concerned."

#4063. Feature: 60+ PS5, PS4 Games to Buy in PS Store's Huge Black Friday Sale (North America/Europe)

PS5 and PS4 games going cheap we recommend

The PS Store's Black Friday sale is on now, running until 30th November, 2026 — with a mid-sale refresh planned for the 16th.

As with nearly every offer in Sony's digital store, there are literally thousands of PS5 and PS4 games going cheap. Obviously, nobody has the time to scroll through all those deals, which is where this guide (hopefully) comes in handy.

We've put together a list of some of the games we'd highly recommend while they're on offer.

Everything listed here comes with at least a 7/10 score from Push Square, and every game is at its lowest price point, with some setting new lows in this sale.

Discounted prices are shown in bold, and games at a new lowest-ever price are bold and underlined.

If you need to top up your PSN wallet, we've got you covered:

Please note that some external links on this page are affiliate links, which means if you click them and make a purchase we may receive a small percentage of the sale. Please read our FTC Disclosure for more information.

Let's have a look at some of the best games in the Black Friday sale.

1000xRESIST is all in on story, and this laser focus allows it to tell one of the most captivating and intriguing experiences you can have in video games. This sci-fi adventure sees an alien disease almost wipe out humanity, but one person is immune, and they rebuild society underground by cloning her. Combining visual novel elements with exploration, it's not the most challenging game to play, but its narrative more than makes it worthwhile.

If you're looking for a chilled out puzzle game to wind down with, A Monster's Expedition comes highly recommended. It's one of those puzzlers with a seemingly straightforward set of mechanics, but it uses them in increasingly smart ways to really test your brainpower. Set across hundreds of tiny islands you need to navigate by pushing logs into the water, its forgiving nature and gentle presentation make it a lovely game to get lost in.

A whimsical, miniature open world awaits in A Short Hike. From a top-down perspective, you explore an island with lots of interesting places to visit and adorable characters, each of whom has a task for you. This laid back experience is a true joy as you gain new abilities, collect things, and discover new areas.

Absolum is both a brilliantly crafted beat-'em-up and a devilishly addictive roguelike. Although the overall experience does feel slightly short-lived, you'll seriously struggle to tear yourself away from the game's striking fantasy world — especially when all of its systems start to click.

Arranger: A Role-Puzzling Adventure is a delightfully inventive puzzle game that weaves in a neat narrative to pull you through. Playing as a character that literally moves the world around her as she goes, this is effectively a series of slide puzzles set within a fleshed out world full of whimsical character. Always building on its core idea in imaginative ways, this is brilliant fun from start to finish.

Building upon the great foundations laid in Astro's Playroom, Astro Bot is the full-blown 3D platformer the little robot deserves. It's an explosion of creativity and fun; there is something new to discover in practically every level, and all of it is purpose built to put a smile on your face. Not only is it bursting with imagination, it's also executed brilliantly. The controls are spot on, every new mechanic and power-up is fun to use, and it's all presented with incredibly sharp visuals and flawless performance. The icing on the cake is its celebration of PlayStation's past 30 years, with delightful nods to hundreds of classics. We can't recommend this highly enough.

While many of the included games may border on unplayable from a modern perspective, the painstaking attention to detail in Atari 50: The Anniversary Celebration is extremely easy to appreciate. The museum-like carousel of content, from interviews through to original artwork, is presented so handsomely that you can’t not get swept up in Atari’s dramatic story. And the fact that there over 100 of the company’s most famous titles, emulated excellently with their original instruction manuals available to pore over, adds playable context to a lot of the content. This is just an impressive overall experience that will appeal to those who lived through the rise (and fall) of Atari, as well as younger players eager to learn a little more about one of the industry’s true pioneers.

Ball X Pit is a dangerously addictive roguelite that combines the speedy runs and rapid leveling up of Vampire Survivors with the ball-bouncing action of Breakout. It's one of those concepts that'll make you question why a game like it hasn't been done before, because it works brilliantly. Every element of the game feeds into something else, and the result is this incredibly compelling game that has a surprising amount to see and do.

Battle Chef Brigade Deluxe is the definitive version of this unusual but great culinary adventure. Set in a world where chefs go head-to-head in a prestigious cooking tournament, the game is half action title and half cooking minigames. You'll go out slaying monsters and harvesting ingredients, then brew them up to create delicious dishes to satisfy the judges. It's an odd recipe, but results in a surprisingly tasty dish.

A true cult classic, Beyond Good & Evil: 20th Anniversary Edition is a lovely remaster of a PS2 favourite. Playing as freedom fighter Jade, this unique sci-fi adventure has you exploring a weird and wonderful world through the lens of her camera. The remaster brings the visuals up to date and throws in some quality-of-life improvements, but the main reason to play this is for the great story and characters, which remain fresh and charming to this day.

Broken Sword: Shadow of the Templars is a sacred text in the history of point-and-click adventure games, and new remaster Reforged is the best version of the game that's ever been released. Quality-of-life improvements mean players who just want to enjoy the story without too much lateral thinking can do so, while veterans of the genre or returning fans can play the game in its original form, goats and all. Paris in the fall has never been more beautiful.

There have been climbing games before, but Cairn is a really unique example. To scale the huge Mount Kami, you need to control Aava's limbs individually, looking out for the best holds as you inch upward. On top of the challenging, physics-based mountaineering, you also need to keep on top of her health and hunger, but these survival aspects never feel too overbearing. It's a nicely balanced game with climbing that feels tangible and realistically tough.

Half interactive story, half cube-based puzzler, Catherine: Full Body is the expanded remaster of Atlus' brilliantly weird take on love. You play as Vincent, a 32-year-old bachelor who can't quite decide if he wants to commit to his long-term girlfriend. His potential infidelity gives way to suspiciously vivid nightmares where he's forced to scramble up towers made of blocks, lest he wake up dead. It's as mental as it sounds, but the tactile puzzles are addictive, and the storytelling is gripping at its best.

From the makers of TowerFall Ascension, Celeste is a pure platformer that provides a stern challenge. Using a straightforward set of moves, it does a lot with very little, but it's not just gameplay where it impresses. Madeline's climb up Celeste Mountain is both literal and metaphorical as she struggles to overcome her inner demons. Wonderfully pairing a touching story with rock solid platforming, this is one indie adventure that'll stay with you.

Creaks is one of PS4's very best puzzle games. Its commitment to continually evolving its mechanics makes for a phenomenal puzzling experience packed full of surprises and elating moments. With a stunning art style to boot as well as a narrative which reveals itself in all the right ways, Creaks offers an unforgettable ride that can be considered truly special.

Some say there are too many Metroidvania games for this world, yet when one as good as Crypt Custodian comes along, it serves as a reminder of exactly why so many developers chase that addictive fusion of explorative action. With shades of Death's Door and Tunic, brotherly duo Kyle and Eric Thompson have made an approachable yet exceedingly enjoyable adventure full of combat, platforming, puzzles, and charm.

Stephen has been part of the Push Square team for over six years, bringing boundless enthusiasm and a deep knowledge of video games to his role as Assistant Editor. Having grown up playing every PlayStation console to date, he's developed an eclectic taste, with particular passion for indie games, arcade racers, and puzzlers. He's also our go-to guy for Sonic-related matters, much to his delight/chagrin.

#4061. Bandai Namco Reveals Its Involvement On Zelda: Ocarina Of Time

Just recently, Xenoblade Chronicles developer Monolith Soft revealed its involvement on Zelda: Ocarina of Time for Switch 2, confirming that it contributed to various aspects including "game design, programming, and graphics".

Monolith's involvement isn't a huge surprise given it's previous work on other Zelda titles, but another company has now spoken up to confirm its own involvement: Bandai Namco.

Taking to its official website, Bandai Namco revealed it helped out with various visual elements of the game ahead of its release on 5th November 2026:

"We were commissioned to create some of the visual assets and artwork, including characters, terrain, animations, cutscenes, and UI, for the Nintendo Switch™ 2 game "The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time," released by Nintendo Co., Ltd. on November 5, 2026."

Of course, the primary developer for Ocarina of Time is Nintendo itself, with Hokwai Ng serving as director, with Eiji Aonuma and Hidemaro Fujibayashi on board as producers. We might be jumping the gun here, but we suspect Fujibayashi-san, who directed both Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom, is likely helming the next mainline game.

In a recent interview, Aonuma-san stated that the reason behind the assignment of HokWai Ng was his ability to "solve problems aggressively". He also presented some interesting ideas for future projects, prompting Aonuma to view him as the ideal candidate to helm Ocarina of Time.

#4060. The Death Stranding Series Has Been Played By Way More People Than You'd Expect

The two Death Stranding games have been modest sellers since their launches, generating more sales than most AAA titles, but not on the same level as other console-defining experiences.

According to official numbers, the first game sold over five million copies. Sales stats relating to the sequel have never been shared, but analyst estimates suggested 1.4 million units were sold during its first few days on the market. In the years since their releases, these totals will have only gone up.

Now we have a new milestone, though, as revealed by Kojima Productions: the Death Stranding series has been played by over 28 million people.

In a social media post to celebrate the first game's seventh anniversary, Hideo Kojima posted a graphic confirming "28 million Porters worldwide". That is 28 million players, not 28 million sales. The image clarifies the total encompasses all console and PC versions of the two games, and anyone who has played them on a subscription service.

Of course, the first Death Stranding started out as a PS4 exclusive, but then made its way to PC less than a year after launch. A Director's Cut version for PS5 then arrived in September 2021, and then in 2024, the game really expanded its availability: it released on iOS, Amazon Luna, and Xbox Series X|S.

The first game is also available on PS Plus Extra, which will be one of the subscription services helping to boost the player numbers.

As for Death Stranding 2, it's just on PS5 and PC for now.

Two of the defining games for the PS4 and PS5 generations, I awarded a rare 10/10 score to both games upon their releases. For the first game, I said: "Death Stranding doesn’t raise the bar for any particular genre, it creates an entirely new one."

Kojima Productions expanded on that original idea with the sequel: "In what will prove to be one of the defining games of the PS5 generation, Death Stranding 2: On the Beach is a profound achievement of design, gameplay, narrative, and visuals. As all four meet in the middle, Kojima Productions has crafted a cinematic spectacle that flawlessly transitions between action and traversal, all wrapped up in the most absorbing of narratives."

Welcome to today's edition of pedantry corner:

As any maths fans will tell you, the conclusion of 28 million people is unwarranted. As that figure combines all sales and streaming it does not allow for the fact that the same person could have played on two or more different formats. It is also a fair assumption that a large proportion of Death Stranding 2 players also played the first game and have therefore been counted twice.

All we can fairly say is that up to 28 million people have played (and it is probably closer to half of that).

Of course any physical copy could be enjoyed by a limitless number of people. So the real number could actually be in the trillions.

#4059. Nicolas Cage is glad Spider-Noir only got one season because his "high-risk" performance could "wear out [its] welcome"

Join the GamesRadar community for quick access. Enter your email below and we'll send confirmation, and sign you up to our newsletter.

Nicolas Cage is happy Spider-Noir was a one-and-done show

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Spider-Noir was unceremoniously cancelled by Amazon earlier this year just weeks after the release of the first season. For most, this was bad news. However, star Nicolas Cage sees the silver lining, as he worried his "high-risk" performance as web-slinging P.I. Ben Reilly could "wear out its welcome."

Speaking to IGN on the Madden red carpet, Cage reiterated that he's happy to leave Reilly and the world of Spider-Noir behind, in part because he considers it a "perfect season" of TV, and in part because of the possibility that his performance could get tired.

"You never want to get stuck repeating a character and wear out your welcome," Cage said. "Ben Reilly is so idiosyncratic. I was doing something that was pretty high-risk, tightrope stuff. You do that season 2, season 3, and you could really wear out your welcome. So when they didn't pick it up, I was like, 'Phew!' I love that character, and I love that season, and it will always be there, and it will always be fresh."

Cage has only reprised characters a handful of times across his career, and seems far more comfortable breaking new ground, which is how you end up with off-beat performances like Ben Reilly in the first place, which Cage described as a "Spider pretending to be a person." Genius.

There are other, more material, reasons why Spider-Noir was cancelled, despite racking up 11 Emmy nominations. It was reportedly extremely expensive, costing in the region of $400 million for 8 episodes, making it one of the most expensive seasons of TV ever. The show's solid – but not spectacular – viewership simply wasn't enough to justify the expense. Cage also refused to sign an A.I. waiver while making Spider-Noir, and doesn't think he'll work with Amazon again as a result.

The show was well-received, hitting 92% on Rotten Tomatoes, though our own Spider-Noir review was more measured, awarding the alt-universe Spider-Man show 3.5 stars. Before it was cancelled, showrunner Oren Uziel teased that season 2 could see Ben Reilly in the midst of World War 2: "Obviously, as time passes from 1933, we’re heading towards not just trouble in the financial markets in New York, but also a geopolitical struggle that would be an amazing canvas for any future storytelling."

Spider-Noir may be no more in live-action, but don't be surprised to see him pop up in next year's Spider-Man: Beyond the Spider-Verse. And Amazon reportedly has four more Spider-Man variant shows in development, so there should be plenty of web-swinging action on screen again soon enough.

Spider-Noir is streaming now on Prime Video. Look ahead with our guide on all the most exciting upcoming shows left in the year.

#4058. Fewer genAI clones of "someone else's specific game" should flood the net going forwards, as Anthropic tell Claude to stop messing with some stuff other people own

It will still let people generate "original" games using the tech

Anthropic have told their genAI tool Claude to start ducking requests from users to recreate or clone existing games, following a flood of folks using the tech to generate six-fingered remakes. Instead of risking infringing on the intellectual property of series or titles that companies which aren't Anthropic own, Claude will instead restrict itself to only generating "original" games slopped together based on whatever data it's drawing on.

"We added two sentences to Claude Code's prompt on Opus 5.5 to steer it away from recreating someone else's specific game because using Claude to infringe IP is against our usage policy," Anthropic staffer Addy Osmani wrote on not Twitter in response to a rando with a cat profile picture having spotted the change.

"Original games, genre games, and games built from your own designs and assets are meant to keep working," Osmani continued. "We'll continue to iterate to ensure we're striking the right balance. In the meantime, if Claude turns down something that's yours, send it my way." Game Developer reached out to Anthropic for confirmation and were pointed to Osmani's post.

The change should make it harder to add to the horde of genAI-powered decomps, recomps, and ports which have hit the net recently. It's hardly a surprising one, given studios like Bethesda have seemingly had to take matters into their own lawyers' hands to get the likes of an AI-generated Fallout game taken offline, with games that've just been ripped wholesale or barely tweaked likely on even more perilous ground. That said, not every corp's responded to the DIY decompilation craze by immediately taking legal action.

There's a serious degree of irony to Anthropic slapping Claude and telling it stealing is bad. One of the ways the company develop and train their genAI models is by scraping publicly available data from the internet via a web crawler.

So, some nicking of stuff is bad, little bot people keep asking to regurgitate stuff into slop they can then try to pass off as something they've created. But not all nicking of stuff, lest our whole business be on rather shaky ground.

It's unlikely this move from Anthropic does much to convince actual developers of original games they're safe to put demos of their games out prior to release, without risking dickheads using genAI to clone said demo and potentially release a slop version in rapid fashion, but one can dream of that genie being put back in the bottle someday.

Super Smash Bros. and Kirby creator Masahiro Sakurai isn't thinking about retirement, as people still want him to make games.

Masahiro Sakurai confirmed back in 2022 that he is "semi-retired," whatever that means, which was roughly one year after Sora was released as the final Super Smash Bros. Ultimate DLC character, bringing an end to nine years of straight development that started with Super Smash Bros. for Wii U and 3DS in 2012. This was followed by a YouTube channel he ran for two years and by Kirby Air Riders, a Nintendo Switch 2 exclusive that released a year ago.

Speaking at the Famitsu 40th Anniversary Festival (translated by Genki_JPN), Sakurai was asked about retirement, saying that as long as there is demand, or he can meet that demand, he won't consider it time to hang it up. He says, "Unfortunately, I’m still working at full throttle." And while there's been no confirmation of what he's up to, it's probably the next Super Smash Bros.

However, Sakurai says he has noticed a decline in some parts of his body, and his eyes are tiring far more easily. During that long Super Smash Bros. development, Sakurai suffered from calcific tendonitis but kept working on the game regardless. He notes that, because the demand for him to create remains, the only question left is "when will my spirit break?" He admits that it's "certainly not the case" when asked whether it's okay for him to maintain this workload, but that he's always thinking about what he can do for the games industry. He recently retired his Game Designers Award after 16 years due to being unable to find a successor, which should hopefully cut down on his workload a bit.

#4055. Rumour: Samsung's New Chip Process Kicks Off 'Nintendo Switch 2 Lite' Speculation

Update: Digital Foundry weighs in on the rumour

Update [Mon 9th Nov 2026, 4:45pm]: At the end of last month, we covered a rumour that Nintendo was working on a 'Switch 2 Lite' model that would supposedly utilise a new chip process in the works at Samsung.

We clarified at the time that it was all nothing more than a rumour, and now the tech experts over at Digital Foundry have popped up to add their ten cents' worth to the conversation. Unsurprisingly, they don't have a whole lot of faith in the idea.

The biggest reason for the outlet's dismissal is the lack of any solid sourcing that Nintendo is looking to downsize its hardware in the first place. "The existence of Samsung materials for a new process that could be used for a handheld doesn't say much on its own," DF says, claiming that the rumoured specs look "more like guesswork".

Then there's the technical side of things, with DF noting that Switch 2 already uses a bespoke processor, so it's not like the transition to the new 8LPU+ would come easily. On top of that, it deems the chip process' rumoured 15% drop in power consumption as "nice to have, but doesn't yield the transformative battery improvements required for a smaller revision" — the original jump from Switch to Switch Lite roughly halved power consumption, let's not forget.

Still, the rumour remains exactly that, a rumour, for the time being. Samsung should spill the beans on the new process next month, but until then, it might be best to continue taking everything with a pinch of salt.

News Is Switch 2 Lite Possible, Thanks to New Samsung Chip Technology?

Digital FoundrySpecs have appeared online, but something doesn't make sense.

Original Story: Samsung reportedly has a new chip in the works that could help make dreams of a 'Switch 2 Lite' a reality (thanks for the heads up, Notebook Check).

As shared on Bluesky by Nintendo Patents Watch, Samsung has supposedly been working on a new 8LPU+ chip process which might be able to assist with making the Nvidia chip inside Switch 2 more compact and more powerful, while drawing on less power.

While the chip itself hasn't been officially revealed yet (South Korean outlet Electronic Times reports that it could be unveiled in December), the word on the street is that the chip process will boast a 12% performance enhancement, 15% power reduction, and an 8% area shrink, among other features, making it a prime candidate for, we don't know, a smaller console.

At the IEDM 2026, Samsung is scheduled to present its 2nd-gen 8nm process 8LPU+: • 12% performance enhancement • 15% power reduction • 8% area shrink • ~10% I/O area reduction • Stand-by leakage reduction Is this Nvidia and Nintendo’s plan all along for the Switch 2 Lite? 1/

With Samsung behind the custom Nvidia chip already in the Switch 2, there's every chance that the new tech could also be used in Nintendo's favour. A smaller Switch 2 — perhaps borrowing the portable-first, non-dock USPs of its predecessor's Lite model — might even pose a cheaper alternative for those wanting to get in on the new hardware's exclusives. With rising costs on just about everything (particularly in the tech space), a less powerful Switch 2 model with cheaper components sure does sound appealing.

We've also got to remember that Nintendo is wrapping up Switch 1 distribution in February 2027. It doesn't necessarily mean that something will be coming in to replace it, we should point out, but if Nintendo and Samsung do have something in the works, it'd be a prime time to introduce it. Heck, the original Switch Lite was released a mere two and a half years after the base model, so who's to say Nintendo doesn't have a Switch 2 equivalent in store for late 2028?

Of course, we've already seen the smallest Switch 2 revision already this year, with the replaceable battery model being introduced in Europe. Rumblings of an 'OLED model' remain under the surface as ever, but what if a 'Lite' option pops up first? Only time will tell, eh!

#4054. Fix up towering robots while battle rages outside in Bay 12: Mech Repair, a first-person job sim with some handsome heavy duty analog tech

The most important thing to know about Bay 12: Mech Repair is that these are mechs of the MechWarrior or possibly Patlabor school – that is, basically WW2 tanks on hydraulic legs, with cockpits full of switches and wireframe displays. Their bodies are assemblages of pistons and reactors. They are not biomechs like the ones in Evangelion. An Evangelion Repair game would be… different. Less industrial, more Oedipal. You would dread removing the smallest piece of housing.

Which isn't to say that Bay 12: Mech Repair represents life on Easy Street, exactly. There's a big war happening outside, its fortunes palpable in the minced leg joints and pocked torsos of the war-bots lowered into your hangar. You're also fed details about the lives of pilots when you accept a work order. Lieutenant Iona Vale of the 3rd Recon Company says there's "left leg hesitation after extended operation", especially at higher temperatures. That sure sounds like a thing that could get Lieutenant Iona Vale killed.

It's not clear whether you can diagnose faults incorrectly, and shape the progress of the conflict, but the context brings extra emotional charge to what might otherwise be a cosy process of glueing together very expensive Air-Fix models, for all the sense of scale.

Bay 12: Mech Repair follows a familiar flow, as job sims go. Banged-up Iron Giants arrive in a steady procession. You figure out what's wrong with them based on scans, pilot reports, and so forth. Then you get out there with a welder, drill and spanner to make it right. Busted parts can be salvaged for scrap for custom components. Completed work orders net you credits that must be divided between restocking your inventory and buying new tools.

You also have the option of clearing away rust and applying a new paintjob. I'm fascinated to know if this has any real impact on either the story or your fortunes, because I guarantee that I am going to spend far more time obsessing over dazzle camouflage than giving the ol' actuators a haircut.

Read more on Steam. The devs, Crimson Herring Studios, are them wot did Sovereign Syndicate, an apparently decent Victorian fantasy RPG that we never found time to review. Look, I am not made of thumbs and eyeballs. As for the daunting possibility of an Evangelion Fixing Sim, the recently announced Valkyrie Iteration gets into some of the squirming detail, there.
