#4053. Making a $300 PS5 Instead of a $1,200 PS6 Would Be 'True Innovation', Says Ex-PlayStation Boss

As the PS5 generation approaches its sixth year, talk of what comes next has been circulating for a while, and with hardware as pricey as it is, the prospect of a PS6 isn't as exciting as it perhaps should be.

Opinion differs on that, of course, but it's generally accepted that Sony's next-gen machine is going to be eye-wateringly expensive, and it's currently anyone's guess as to whether it'll be worth a purchase.

Shawn Layden, formerly CEO of PlayStation and head of PlayStation Studios, has weighed in on the matter of next generation console hardware in a new interview.

Speaking on the Trophy Room podcast, he says Sony's best move wouldn't be to create a pricey, brand new console, it would be to revise the current hardware in order to sell it cheaper.

"The typical runway for platforms [is] six to eight years, you get a new one," Layden says. "But typically, that new one brought you something mind-blowing."

He speaks about the various innovative leaps from one console to the next, concluding that the move from PS4 to PS5 was mostly led by raytracing and teraflops. He expects technical aspects like this will be used to sell PS6 as well, but says these are "differences only dogs can hear", implying diminishing returns.

"We have enough power in the machine. The innovation needs to come not from making PS6 for $1200, it's to make another PS5 for $300. Now that would be true innovation."

As Layden points out, the current generation is the first to go up in price rather than down, and he thinks continuing with a PS6 at such a premium price point, and focusing on incremental increases in power, risks alienating the audience.

"What the company needs to do is do what it's never done, which is, don't iterate the console," he says. "Make it smaller, make it cheaper, do all the things you can around that. The silicon is fine, the OS is fine. It's more than enough power to build the kind of games all of us want to play."

While his words of wisdom may ring true for many, Sony itself is forging ahead with its next-gen plans, so we'll likely be faced with a costly new console within the next couple of years.

#4052. Indiana Jones returnee John Rhys-Davies was "very disappointed" with Dial of Destiny

Join the GamesRadar community for quick access. Enter your email below and we'll send confirmation, and sign you up to our newsletter.

The Sallah actor airs his grievances against Dial of Destiny

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

John Rhys-Davies, who returned to the Indiana Jones franchise to reprise his role as Sallah, has described Dial of Destiny as a "disappointing film."

"I'll be honest with you, I was very disappointed in it," Rhys-Davies told Off/Frame.

A post shared by OFFFRAME.com (@offframe_com)

For Rhys-Davies, Dial of Destiny – which brought back Harrison Ford as Indy at the age of 80 – should have played the hits instead of introducing a wave of new characters.

"The film is meant to be a nostalgia film," Rhys-Davies lamented. "They filled the cast up with people we had never met before – so there can be no nostalgia, really."

Other complaints Rhys-Davies harbored about Dial of Destiny include having his role as Sallah supposedly cut down (he only had a handful of scenes) and the treatment of Antonio Banderas' character Renaldo, who is killed off within minutes of appearing.

"I found that the scenes I'd been promised in the thing were cut immediately [after] I signed the contract. I think it's a disappointing film. What is tragic, really, is… [Antonio] Banderas. The most exciting actor of his generation… but what a terrible thing to do to him," Rhys-Davies said.

Dial of Destiny was largely seen as a disappointment, grossing under $400 million at the box office, the lowest in franchise history. Its 71% Rotten Tomatoes score also reveals a mixed critical response to the fifth Indiana Jones movie.

Speaking earlier this year to Deadline, former Lucasfilm president Kathleen Kennedy said there were "no regrets" over Dial of Destiny but there was no interest "right now" in making another Indy adventure.

"I have no regrets about that because Harrison [Ford] wanted to do that more than anything. He did not want Indy to end with the fourth movie," Kennedy said. "He wanted a chance at another, and we did that for him. I think that was the right thing to do."

#4051. You can make a vampire hunter who's afraid of the dark, disease and small spaces in Hunter: The Reckoning - Deathwish, and that's surely the best way to play

A month or two back I penned a 1500 word whine about feeling too powerful in Blood of Dawnwalker. "Gimme a vampire sim in which I'm a pathetic vein-nibbling goblin," I wrote, using many more adjectives than that. Well, never let it be said that I'm biased against vampires, for I am equally keen to play an RPG in which I am the least capable vampire hunter in the universe. A vampire hunter who screams when he wakes up with his hair over his face. A vampire hunter who has to spray the vampires with antibac before staking them.

An RPG like Hunter: The Reckoning – Deathwish, perhaps, which presents you with a choice of Advantages and Flaws when creating a character. You have to balance these out on a gnarly weighing scale, before they'll let you through the game's front door. Here is a video showing all that off, together with a lot of sixpacks.

The Advantage/Flaw system looks familiar on the surface. Advantages include Warrior, which gives you +15% chance of a critical hit, or Charmer, which gives you a +1 to Persuasion skill checks. Flaws include clumsy, bad reputation, fear of darkness, hypochondriac, and claustrophobia.

I don't know much about the tabletop game on which Deathwish is based, and the video skims the detail here, but I suspect the last three Flaws will boil down to something like "-1 Constitution in Unlit Closets". Still, I really enjoy the idiocy of going up against crypt-dwelling undead while being unable to tolerate shadows, small spaces, and disease. In general, I'd love it if Hunter: The Reckoning – Deathwish steered well away from any possibility of simply overpowering the vamps, to say nothing of the werewolves and other creatures of the night.

This appears to be the idea: devs Teyon have stressed their desire to make something more story and investigation-driven, after the stomping gibfest that was RoboCop: Rogue City. As narrative designer Mateusz Działowski put it in a previous dev diary, they've "switched from action with RPG elements into RPG with action elements". Amongst other things, you'll need to put together a team of fellow would-be slayers, each with secrets and traumas, and gather clues about best tactics while roaming the game's condensed and shiny New York City. You can read more about it all on Steam.

The TV adaptation is apparently still moving forward

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The headwinds of the industry led to the closure of BioWare recently, and the latent Mass Effect 5 – known internally as Mass Effect Universe – went with it. We may never know exactly what the devs were putting together for the sequel, but details are dripping out, the latest being that it would've tied into the planned Amazon TV show in some way.

Michael Gamble, former project director and executive producer at BioWare, addresses a fan on Twitter asking if the Mass Effect Universe plot would be used for the show. "Both are meant to compliment each other," he responds.

That's a fascinating wrinkle. It seems like the two productions were collaborating together to some degree, if only to keep each other informed of their narrative intentions. Among the other titbits we've learned about the fifth Mass Effect is the notion that it would've involved a multiverse.

According to Gamble the plot from Mass Effect Universe and the TV show were supposed to compliment each other. If the show is still happening this may be our only hope #SaveMassEffect https://t.co/hY7pQtcA0zNovember 8, 2026

Apparently you would've been able to jump across timelines somehow. The exact mechanics for how are unknown, but on top of anything else, this means every possible outcome from the original trilogy is technically canon. Clever, because I lowkey dreaded seeing the discourse tear itself open once everyone saw which of the endings from Mass Effect 3 BioWare favored.

Details of what's going on with the TV adaptation are scant. Amazon and MGM announced the production back in 2024, and progress has been slow since. However, reports have emerged that it's still on the docket and moving forward, with showrunners Doug Jung and Daniel Casey in tow.

When we see it is anyone's guess. Thankfully, we're at a point where many video game adaptations have proven lucrative, which means the likelihood this quietly disappears is smaller. Gamble's comment is being shared around with the idea that gives hope to saving Mass Effect.

I'm not sure about that, but at least the franchise will live on in some form. It's ironic really, since one of the reasons I fell in love with the first game is that it felt like the Star Trek RPG I hadn't gotten before. Now it might just be the new Star Trek show I've been yearning for.

#4049. Guide: Xbox Game Pass Essential: Full List Of Games (November 2026 Update)

Here's everything you can play on Game Pass Essential

Back in 2023, Microsoft finally phased out Xbox Live Gold, replacing it with Xbox Game Pass Core as a new entry-level tier to its subscription service. Since then, it's been renamed to Xbox Game Pass Essential as of October 2025.

We've gathered together the full Xbox Game Pass Essential list of titles down below, and we'll continue to update this guide as Microsoft adds more games to the library. Microsoft says all Essential titles are "fully playable" on both console and PC (despite the Xbox website suggesting only around half are PC-enabled), and a lot of them are supported as part of Xbox Cloud Gaming too.

"Our revamped Essential plan now includes unlimited cloud gaming, online multiplayer, in-game benefits, and Rewards with Xbox, plus a curated catalog of 50+ games playable on both console and PC. The Essential library is now fully playable on PC, featuring standout titles like Hades, Cities: Skylines – Remastered, Stardew Valley, and Warhammer 40,000: Darktide. You also get unlimited cloud gaming, allowing you to play games, including select games you own, on the devices you choose — giving you more freedom to play your way."

Before we get into it, we should mention that Xbox classes various free-to-play games as part of the Xbox Game Pass Essential library (because they feature in-game benefits as part of the service), but we're just going to focus on the paid titles that are included with the program.

Here the list of every Xbox Game Pass Essential title so far (as of November 2026):

#4048. Poll: Which Zelda: Ocarina Of Time HUD Option Is Your Favourite?

Just like the open-world entries that precede it, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on Switch 2 comes with a handful of HUD options, so you can play with as much or as little on-screen information as you please.

In our first few hours with the game, we played around with all three of these options, getting to grips with the pros and cons of all of them. Most of us settled on one after a little while, and now we're keen to see where you lovely lot have ended up.

As a reminder, there are three different HUD options in the settings menu's 'In-Game Interface Tab': Normal, Pro, and Master. The first of these is listed as your "Standard display," with your mini map, item selection, D-pad options, life/magic meters, and button prompts all appearing on the screen. It offers the most information you can get at a glance, but it can look a little cluttered for some.

The 'Pro' option tones things down a little, displaying "minimal information," according to its settings definition. This one does away with almost all the info we mentioned above, but button prompts (for 'Talk' or 'Grab' selections) and Navi's speech bubbles still make an appearance. This is a ripe choice for anyone who knows their Zelda mechanics, but still wants to know when something is there to be interacted with.

'Master' mode is the most stripped back of the bunch, offering a "display with no information". This means that everything other than the main gameplay is removed from the screen, and no prompts crop up as you approach NPCs or interactive items. And yes, that includes your targeting cursor. This option keeps things stripped back to the bare minimum and arguably provides the most immersive experience of the bunch, but there's every chance that you'll miss the odd detail (or Navi quip) along the way.

Each setting has its perks, to be sure, and we're not about to say that any one of them is the 'correct' way to play, but still, we're interested to know what mode you have been rocking with so far.

You can let us know your preferred HUD option in the following poll, then take to the comments to let us know why it's stuck.

Which option have you been maining? Let us know in the comments.

#4047. GTA 6 PS5 Physical Edition Includes a Poster, But It's Still Not the Map

Retailers are beginning the process of shipping out their boxed copies of GTA 6, which include a digital download code instead of a physical disc. As they receive their stock, it's now been confirmed there is actually a poster inside the case.

However, it's still not the map of the game world previous GTA games have shipped with.

UK retailer The Game Collection has been able to confirm there's a double-sided A3 poster included in the case, as it plans to ship boxed versions later this week. Those who do get the physical version can start preloading the digital edition ready for release on 19th November 2026.

With physical copies now out in the wild, the contents have been posted online, and the poster included has the GTA 6 key art on one side, and the cover girl on the other:

News GTA 6's PS5 Physical Edition Revealed in First Photo

Guide GTA 6 Release Times and Preload: When Can You Start Playing?

If you want that physical map of the GTA 6 open world, then you'll need to wait until after release. Rockstar has revealed a map poster will be available from its official online store. It's $0.99 if you just want to buy it, or it'll be included free of charge with a purchase of anything else on the storefront.

Preload of GTA 6 will be going live worldwide within the next 24 hours, allowing you to download its 212GB of data well ahead of time. Refer to our GTA 6 Release Times and Preload guide for more information, with the PS5 launch scheduled for 19th November 2026.

#4046. itch.io will soon let you filter games with genAI disclosures out of your search results on the site, after admitting it was previously "critically lacking"

itch.io has unfortunately, much like Steam, long had an issue with genAI content being uploaded in droves, drowning out perfectly good games made by human hands. The apparent standard method against this, voluntary genAI disclosure, has been itch's primary tool to combat this wave of low-quality slop, but hasn't worked out too well; itch revealed a few days ago that 'the number of game pages being created per-day has doubled in the past two months'. Now, in attempts to further combat this, beyond just game assets requiring a genAI disclosure to upload as they have for two years, itch will be expanding the mandatory disclosure to tabletop games, books, comics, and soundtracks, as well as adding a 'no AI' filter directly into the search function.

itch noted in this announcement that its previous moderation of genAI use in projects had been "critically lacking", presumably referring to the unfathomable exponential increase in games being uploaded in the past few months by people who don't give a fuck about creating anything themselves and happily contribute to the death of the planet. itch went on to post "Just deleted a couple terabytes of ai slop" which, I mean, sure, cool! And, look, as many, many people in itch's replies have pointed out, this is not the same as outright banning AI.

Unfortunately, my question at that point becomes: how? itch is not Steam, not a storefront backed by a gigantic corporation with support staff and quality assurance (which, you know, hasn't helped Steam much either). itch is one full-time employee with several contractors and volunteers. If there is a site-wide ban on genAI, people who use genAI will just start lying and sneaking it into their projects anyway. So, then, users just report the offenders, surely? This then requires a manual verification system, which, as is suggested by the sheer amount of games being uploaded every day, is just not feasible, let alone for a team as small as itch. And, frankly, I don't have a better solution here! This is fucked! What itch is doing is, currently, kinda the best it can right now?

itch is a beautiful thing that allows for people who just want to start making games, making art, making music, making books, to have a free space to share it with the world, and gain eyes on their work as well as necessary feedback to improve. It's less of a store and more of a forum for creators and self-published games to interact, guide one another to new, niche, cool shit. Hell, I made a visual novel and posted it on there, becoming another one of those millions of people for whom itch is a valuable platform for first creations. To have this vital space on a path to ruin as a result of the same vile tech that is also on the verge of pushing the global economy over a cliff due to its creators being caught in their multi-year lies is not a future I hope for itch. This is a step in the right direction, and one I genuinely hope pans out well for it in the long run.

#4045. "There’s always a night when Rome burns": South Of Midnight director says that Xbox funding it was "unsustainable", at least in hindsight

"I didn’t know exactly when it would be, but I was always worried about it"

Compulsion Games parted ways with former owners Xbox, having landed on the long list of things Microsoft were determined to ditch as part of multi-round mass cuts this year. Now, South of Midnight creative director David Sears has suggested that an eventual pulling of the rug was something he feared throughout the game's development, to the point where he seemingly doesn't think he'd have funded it if he'd been in the shoes of Xbox execs.

In an interview with MinnMax, Sears - who left Compulsion in March 2025 - outlined that ideally games big publishers put out aim to fall into one of two buckets. They either make lots of money or increase the prestige of the brand by becoming cultural touchstones across multiple generations. Obviously doing both is the perfect outcome, but Sears pegged South of Midnight as being more geared towards the latter camp. The likes of Double Fine's Keeper and Obsidian's Pentiment are other games which off the top of my head could be said to fit that same mold. The issue, of course, is that when push comes to shove, it's the games which can show a strong bottom line at any given moment which make the best case for their studios' short term survival if cash is tight.

So, South of Midnight lived in a risky place, with Sears recalling: "I literally told people. I was like, yeah, this could be terrible because somebody is going to say, one day, 'The money tap, we're closing those floodgates' and that's going to have really traumatic results downstream". The interviewer then asked Sears if what he was getting at is that, while he's glad Xbox funded South of Midnight, he might not have done so or at least cut the funding earlier if he was in charge of the console maker.

"Yeah, probably," Sears replied. "I mean, I wanted to make it. No doubt. Obviously, because we made it. Would I have turned off someone else's money flow before South of Midnight? Yeah, because I'm not completely selfless. It just seems like, in hindsight at least, it was unsustainable. So, of course, it was going to have a 'shocking' outcome. I mean, it's easy to dissect it now, right? But at the time, I would talk to other directors and [they] would be like, 'How is this happening? I mean, how did we get so lucky? Is this a golden era?' And I would always be like, 'For now'. There's always a night when Rome burns and I didn't know exactly when it would be, but I was always worried about it."

Notably, Sears added that in his view modern Microsoft showed a "more humane" side than the version of the company that existed in the 90s and early 2000s by giving studios like Compulsion a chance to spin out on their own rather than simply shuttering them outright once they were deemed surplus to requirements.

Given the director's no longer at Compulsion, it seems he'll not have a say on what their next game looks like, but as a newly indie studio one would imagine they'll have a keen eye on the bottom line.

A new Lego Yoshi set is on the way, and based on a few clues, it seems as though it'll be a big one.

Teased via the Nintendo Today app (which provides personalized updates for you based on the games you like), the Lego Yoshi set appears in an extreme close up with the promise that it's "hatching soon." Because this is a for-adults model, it'll be a display piece - presumably a full figure - rather than a playset like the upcoming 2027 range. Some of the best Lego sets so far have been Super Mario collector's items, so the bar is pretty high here.

All we can see of the new kit is its face, with eyes and part of a nose poking out the side of the screen. However, it's possible to guess how large Yoshi will be by the size of the pieces on display... and from what I can tell, it'll be to scale with the Mario and Standard Kart set (which may tell us something about price, because that one's currently $150 on Amazon). The curved pieces with a single stud on the nose are around an inch across at the widest point, for example, so Yoshi's head looks as though it'll be roughly four inches tall. You can then start to work backwards and figure out how big the rest of the model will be.

Using that guestimate and assuming he's standing, I suspect he'll be around a foot or so as a result - e.g. a similar size or just taller than the Lego Piranha Plant set (which used those same curved pieces for its head), but smaller than Lego The Mighty Bowser.

Naturally, all this assumes he isn't on a vehicle like Lego Luigi & Mach 8. If he is, that'll obviously change things because he's sat rather than standing proud. I'm not sure what they'd put him on, but he's often seen on bikes in Mario Kart 8 or the Wild Wiggler kart. Because we've seen a couple of karts already courtesy of Mario and Luigi, I'd quite like to see the franchise's bikes get some love this time around.

First discovered by Vooks, this is a slightly unusual way for Lego to unveil a new set; at the time of writing, you can only find it on the Nintendo Today app. Still, that tease does give us some handy information nonetheless. Judging by the 2027 trademark we know for a fact Lego Yoshi won't be launching this year, for instance.

Even if he doesn't cross the finish line until later, it's still a good time to be a fan of Lego dinosaurs right now; alongside Yoshi, a huge Lego Godzilla kit was revealed last week. While it's changed a lot since the original fan design was submitted, it's still tremendously impressive. Hopefully Yoshi will live up to that.

Sony has updated the PlayStation Portal in Japan, releasing a new handheld that maintains many of the same features as the original, with one key difference. The revised gaming handheld now includes internal storage.

That signals a big shift away from the brand's original vision for the device. The PS Portal we know in the US and UK functions as a remote player first and foremost, streaming PS5 games from a console (or separately via a PlayStation Plus Premium account). It's still one of the best PS5 accessories, but with the PS6 expected to launch alongside its own handheld device, there's one line in Sony's official announcement that brings this internal storage under the microscope.

"With an eye towards future functionality," the PlayStation Japan blog post states, "the new model includes additional internal storage."

It's that future functionality that has ears pricked across the industry this morning. Sony states that more information on this mysterious storage is incoming, with details surrounding the feature still to be "finalized." However, it's one of the first official statements we've had linking Sony's current lineup to its future handheld ambitions.

What that storage will be used for in the existing PS Portal remains a mystery. With no listed upgrades to the internals, it would be pretty difficult to consider Sony running games directly from the Portal handheld in its current state. We also don't know how much extra storage is under the hood.

Just after launch, it was discovered that the existing PlayStation Portal has 6GB of free space floating around. Including the storage upgrade within the announcement, and citing future features, makes it seem like there's a chunkier drive being added - rather than a few extra gigs to support a larger Android OS update.

The new PlayStation Portal launches in Japan only and, like the Midnight Black PS5 announced last month, it's pretty locked down to the region. It can only be set to Japanese language and requires a Japanese PSN account to run. That said, it will be available to pre-order in the region from November 13, at the same ¥39,980 price as the regular model.

#4042. Halo 2 Is 22 Years Old Today, And I'm Gutted The Remake Isn't Happening

Pure Xbox is listening to: Blow Me Away - Breaking Benjamin 🎶

It feels like only yesterday that Halo: Campaign Evolved teased a remake of Halo 2, something I've been hoping for more and more as time went on. After all, it's been 22 long years now. Yep, that's right - Halo 2 launched on November 9, 2004 for the original Xbox, and has often been credited as the game that put Xbox Live on the map.

As the years slip by, anniversaries for OG Xbox titles have a habit of making me feel my age. Still, what a privilege it was to be there for the inception of Xbox Live, to play both co-op and PvP with friends across the globe in the second entry of Bungie's incredible run of Halo games.

Admittedly, it's been a hot-minute since I last booted up Halo 2 in the Master Chief Collection. But visits to retro gaming bars like Manchester's NQ64 reminded me just how good this FPS still is. I recall sitting down for a few games of Slayer, only for the muscle memory to kick in and humble a good number of Hookshot staff - Fraser included. Oh boy, it never gets old.

In fact, just sit back and listen to 15 minutes of Halo 2's main menu music and ponder the good old days of dual-wielding SMGs in Beaver Creek.

Halo 2 took Master Chief's fight against the Covenant to Earth, selling more than 8.4 million copies before its servers shut down in 2010, following the discontinuation of the original Xbox Live services. The game was later ported to PC and remastered for Xbox One as part of Halo: The Master Chief Collection.

Xbox's 25th anniversary is just round the corner: in fact, it's this Sunday! We'll be here, keeping an eye out for any and all announcements from Xbox throughout the week. Understandably, we've been feeling pretty nostalgic, hence this Halo 2 feature. In fact, I'm reinstalling the MCC as we speak.

I was a big fan of Halo Studios' Campaign Evolved. Like, I really, really enjoyed it. So, it's bittersweet knowing that their teased Halo 2 remake in Unreal Engine will never happen.

Sure, the devs fumbled modern Halo multiplayer, but perhaps a Halo 2 remake could have been a case of history repeating itself. Y'know, a remade return of Halo 2's iconic online multiplayer?! Ah, well.

#4040. Arc Raiders devs Embark insist that using genAI for voice lines was necessary, as "actors would just go crazy if they had to read all of that"

Despite taking the voice performances of actors and feeding them into machines to spurt out AI-generated mimicry, Embark CCO Stefan Strandberg insists that "we are not in the industry of replacing actors." In a new video posted to the Arc Raiders channel focused on audio design, Strandberg refers back to the infamous use of genAI in Arc Raiders to generate voice lines based on real voice actors' performances, something which the game was heavily (and rightly) criticised for before and since its release.

In that linked piece (thanks Oisin!), CEO Patrick Söderlund stated that they have been replacing lines that were originally generated with actual recorded lines, presumably because Arc Raiders has made quite a bit of money and now they feel that they can continue paying actors to record more lines, rather than just scraping their talents and avoiding the dreaded fee of paying professionals for their work. This choice already came after their previous game, The Finals, was heavily criticised for the exact same thing, which is just a fascinating series of decisions to consider.

In the video, audio director Bence Pajor explains that the apparent reason for the use of AI was to avoid the "stress" of having to work around actors' availability, as they may be busy working on other projects when Embark decides that a new feature needs new voice lines recorded. Pings, quests, and in-level mission briefings were thus generated using training data based on existing actors' recordings, saving the need to actually get anyone back in a studio or pay them for their time. Citing the amount of variables that the ping system creates, Pajor claims it "becomes too impractical to record every possible version of something. The actors would just go crazy if they had to read all of that", which is a take that falls apart if you consider the simple fact that games of this scope (or bigger) have been managing to work around actors' availability for as long as genAI has not been an accessible technology, which has been almost all of the time that video games have existed. Isn't it crazy that games like Disco Elysium and Baldur's Gate 3 had so, so much recorded dialogue, all without genAI? Or fellow live service shooter Apex Legends, which has been adding and adjusting voice lines via updates for years? How could they possibly have managed it?

Voice actresses Jo Rideout and Diana Gardner, who play Shani and Celeste respectively, are also featured speaking on their characters' relationships as well as their experience working within this hybrid model of recording and generating voices. Gardner notes that "if they only need an hour of my time for a couple call-outs that are short, then I don't have to cancel other shoots or some other project that might also be interesting. So in that way, I feel quite good about it." She then explains that "the contract seemed fair…so it was a no-brainer in that sense. But I didn't know what to expect once I heard the voice come out. I was like, 'Can I take ownership for the performance?' This is hours of work that I've put in, but can I take ownership for the final product? No."

Strandberg goes on to elaborate on his comment on not replacing actors by saying that "We are not in the industry of replacing actors, actually, I think quite the opposite. We should celebrate the performance, and we should give them more space." While Embark's audio team are indeed working on replacing the generated lines with actual performances, that doesn't change the fact that the choice to use AI in the first place was one made simply to save money in not paying actors for their specific work and get the game out the door faster — effectively the 'we'll fix it in post' of games development. While I can respect Garner's awareness that it means she can prioritise other projects when necessary, there is that notable tinge of regret in not being able to take ownership for her hours of work. Fundamentally, Embark has demonstrated its willingness to cut talent to cut costs, seemingly happy to post PR videos implying they had no choice due to the game's scope, and that isn't something a company just goes back on once they realise how 'efficient' it can be.

#4039. Workers & Resources: Soviet Republic's next DLC is set to expand the city building sim into the one place not corrupted by capitalism: SPACE

Following not the inherent liberal capitalistic framework of city builders like SimCity but instead a revolutionary (sorry) interpretation of planning and logistical simulation that prioritises centralisation and minute detail, Hooded Horse and 3DIVISION's Workers & Resources: Soviet Republic offers a tense, socialist look at what a citybuilder could be. Fellow contributor Sin Vega, in her 1.0 review, described it like this: "You have to build things to demolish things. That might be Workers & Resources in a nutshell. You're not managing budgets (money is exclusively for imports/exports), you're organising stuff." Now, having previously expanding out of the Soviet Republic and across the globe with the World Maps DLC, the next step for socialist citybuilding is, of course, space. Our Edwin outright predicted this two years ago, correctly calling that "the logical endgame here is to go to space." Good on him.

The Space Program DLC, set to release on November 23rd, will add a variety of new technologies and types of industry to the builder. It looks like it'll focus on not only the actual rockets that get into space, and the spectacle of it all, but also the huge amounts of science and industry that get to the point of rockets not exploding upon takeoff. For example, while it's all well and good for Space Program's scientists to be able to design rockets that are capable of remaining together for long enough to land safely, the designs they dream of still have to be built, meaning that industrial pipelines must be effectively centralised to ensure that every single component is of high quality and arriving in the required quantity.

The update also specifies the Sputnik and Vostok programs as elements of the expansion, implying a close historical aspect to it — though, elsewhere, "an unprecedented duel with nature" is mentioned, which is referring to either the simple harshness of space or aliens. Jury's out. A 1960s campaign will be a star feature of the DLC, which is described as a place for players to learn the new mechanics "in relative peace, surrounded by a happy, healthy, and economically stable utopia." What an idea.

Stranger Things made the top 10 shows of the last 6 years, but it didn't place as high as you would think

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Even though Stranger Things season 5 came to an end earlier this year, the franchise is kept alive by a fierce fandom that believes the show isn't over. But even with so much support, the sci-fi series still hasn't managed to crack the top five shows of the 2020s.

As reported by Bloomberg in a study from Nielsen, the top ten most-watched TV shows on streaming since 2020 have been revealed. Amassing a whopping 246.55 million minutes watched on streaming is Grey's Anatomy, followed by NCIS, Bluey, Criminal Minds, and Cocomelon. Stranger Things sits in sixth place with 145.24 million minutes viewed. The list continues with Supernatural in seventh place, followed by SpongeBob SquarePants, Family Guy, and The Big Bang Theory.

The list is quite surprising not only because of how low Stranger Things is placed, but because huge shows from the past six years, including House of the Dragon, Wednesday, and so many more, are absent. However, this could just be down to the sheer size of the show in question. Grey's Anatomy has a whopping 23 seasons and 470 episodes, and NCIS has 24 seasons and 511 episodes. Now, that's a lot of minutes.

There is also the rewatchability factor. Medical and police dramas are very rewatchable. You can jump in at any time and can watch whilst folding laundry or starting dinner. The same goes for kids' shows like Bluey and Cocomelon. Stranger Things, on the other hand, requires a little more attention. The sci-fi show still holds popularity on Netflix, though, as seasons 4 and 5 sit in the streamer's top 10 English-language shows of all time, as per Tudum.

Although the main show is seemingly over and done with, Stranger Things lives on as Netflix has multiple spin-offs in the works. There's the second season of the animated show Stranger Things: Tales from '85, and the ' 50s-set prequel series Other Worlds: A Stranger Things Adventure, which is due to hit Netflix in 2028.

Stranger Things is available to watch in its entirety on Netflix. For more, check out our guide to the best Netflix shows, and keep up with new shows on the way.

#4037. Dune 3 fans are sharing their coolest theories about the movies, and you'll never watch them the same way again

These Dune movie theories will make you feel like the Kwisatz-Haderach

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Dune 3 is a little over a month away, and over on social media, fans of the lauded Denis Villeneuve movies have been sharing their "coolest theories". Some of them are so mind-blowing, in fact, that they'll make you feel like you've sipped the Water of Life and can see with absolute prescience.

Responding to a prompt post on X, one of the more popular theories from LULA al gaib is that what we're seeing in Dune is an "alternate timeline of Paul's visions from the books", so both the Frank Herbert novels and Villeneuve movies co-exist in the same universe, despite their differences. This explains the many adaptive changes Villeneuve has made with his movies; for example, why in the novel Paul imagines a timeline where it's him who kills his grandfather, Baron Harkonnen, and not his sister Alia. Paul does kill the Baron in Dune: Part Two, but it's Alia who plunges the knife into her grandfather in the novel.

It's even baked into the text of Dune, as Paul's miraculous abilities as Kwisatz-Haderach allow him to see a number of different timelines. In the movies, we've had a taste of this, as in Part Two, Paul sees visions of Jamis (Babs Olusanmokun) as an ally and friend, even though Jamis is killed by Paul at the climax of Dune: Part One. In Part One, we also see a vision of Chani standing by Paul's side as he unleashes the Fremen on the universe, but we know from the Dune 2 ending that Chani wants nothing to do with genocide and appears to have turned on Paul by Part Three, 19 years later, because of the atrocities being committed in his name.

Another theory from LULA al gaib is equally cool, but a bit of a spoiler for the books if you haven't read beyond Dune: Messiah, so be warned! Ever wondered who that mysterious voice that we first hear in Dune: Part One opening belongs to? What if it wasn't simply a Sardaukar throat-singer, but a descendant of Paul's from thousands of years in the future? Specifically, God Emperor Leto II, who eventually turns into a worm (it's a whole thing). "He would be a kind of 'narrator' and the last historical witness, since he experienced his father Paul Atreides's entire journey through genetic memories." Mind-expanding stuff.

These are all just theories, of course. What we know for certain is that Dune 3 is set to wrap up Villeneuve's trilogy in thrilling fashion, as star Timothée Chalamet has already said he's "absolutely satisfied" with the movie's ending. The final Dune: Part Three trailer released late last month and features plenty of Arrakis action, as well as Robert Pattinson Scytale and Zendaya's Chani trying to kill a maniacal Paul Atreides. And if you're wondering whether Dune 3 can live up to its predecessors, Pattinson has claimed there was a "350-foot-long model of a sandworm" on the set, which sounds pretty next-level to us.

Dune 3 hits theaters on December 18 alongside Avengers: Doomsday. For more, check out our guide to all the upcoming movies in 2026 and beyond.

#4036. I'm sad that the Like A Dragon creator's new studio is closing, but I wish their now-cancelled debut Gang of Dragon wasn't just LAD again

Less than a year after the announcement of their first game, and only four years after the studio's creation, Gang of Dragon developers Nagoshi Studio have been dissolved by a shareholders' resolution (thanks, Gematsu.) That also means a premature end for Gang of Dragon, which was announced at last year's Game Awards with a flashy trailer featuring Like a Dragon-esque realistic visuals, combat and exploration through Kabukicho, a couple new elements like actual gunplay and car chases, as well as the star power of actor Ma Dong-seok (a.k.a. Don Lee). Following reports in March that NetEase, the studio's source of funding, would be pulling said funding in May due to ballooning costs reaching around seven billion yen, the time has sadly come for Nagoshi Studio, having not found any alternative funding sources in the time since.

Gang of Dragon looked very much to be 'just Like a Dragon again', which I find to be something of a depressing fate for a studio headed by the original series' creator. Having left Ryu Ga Gotoku Studio following Judgment and Yakuza: Like a Dragon, two of its most innovative games both with new protagonists and one entirely new turn-based gameplay style, it feels indicative of the industry that Nagoshi was granted funding seemingly on the condition that the studio makes something that just looks like the rest of the Like a Dragon series. I love Ma Dong-seok as an actor, but his presence was one of the more blatant, 'look, we got that guy!' castings of the LAD archetype, which is saying something considering Infinite Wealth had fucking Danny Trejo in a prominent role. The trailer closing with a shot of Dong-seok framed by Kabukicho's torii gate, maybe the most famous image from the Like a Dragon series, put a sour taste in my mouth as being just more of the same brand recognition (yet, for a new IP!) to prioritise safe return on investment.

I'm unfortunately not that surprised to see Gang of Dragon and Nagoshi Studio lost to time, though I am sad about it. I have some conflicted feelings on Nagoshi as a person/auteur, but I don't think he, or his studio, deserves to have funding pulled before they could even release anything as a result of NetEase deciding to pull investments out of non-Chinese companies over time. It's unknown what Nagoshi and the team will be attempting next, but I truly hope they can eventually make something. No More Heroes studio Grasshopper Manufacture was able to detach themselves from NetEase very recently and possibly avoid a similar fate, so it might not be impossible.

#4035. GTA 6: The Festival Is a One-Off Live Music Event, Partly Presented by PlayStation

Rockstar Games has announced GTA 6: The Festival, a special live music event being held to celebrate the launch of the open world action game.

Presented in partnership with PlayStation, the one-off event takes place in Miami, Florida on 21st November, 2026.

"Experience the music of Vice City and Leonida at Grand Theft Auto VI: The Festival, a special live event on November 21 at Mana Wynwood in Miami to celebrate the launch of GTAVI, featuring a star-studded lineup of artists from the game and the official soundtrack."

They will play "nonstop music" across two stages.

If you're interested, you can sign up for the ticket lottery on the official website. The lottery closes at 4pm ET on 10th November, so you don't have long to put your name in the hat.

Ticket prices have not been revealed as yet.

This is just the latest major marketing beat as we lead up to the launch of GTA 6. Most of the bigger events are happening within Miami and Florida, which is of course the real life inspiration for Vice City and Leonida, where the game takes place.

#4034. How To Preload GTA 6 In Full On Xbox Series X|S (Even If You Haven't Bought It)

All 200GB+ goes live in just a few hours' time

The official preload for GTA 6 is literally just a few hours away at the time of writing, and it means everyone will be able to install all 200GB+ of the game on Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S ahead of launch on November 19th.

Here are the official preload / preinstall times for GTA 6 on Xbox Series X|S, as we recently highlighted on Pure Xbox:

News GTA 6 Download Size & Preload Times Officially Revealed For Xbox Series X|S

So, there are two ways to preload GTA 6 on Xbox Series X|S depending on whether you have or haven't bought it yet. If you've pre-ordered the game, payment should have now been taken out of your account, and you'll be able to preload it by going to the Microsoft Store app on your Xbox console and searching for Grand Theft Auto VI.

The page you're looking for is the one in the image at the top of this article, although instead of a "pre-order" button, you should see the ability to install the game if you've bought it already. This will install a 300MB placeholder file until 12am GMT on November 10th, after which time the full 200GB download will become available as an update.

If you run into any issues with this, it's worth doing a restart of your console after the full preload goes live.

"On XBOX Series X|S, pre-loading begins globally on Tuesday, November 10 at 12 a.m. GMT. Code-in-box versions for both consoles should be available from retailers beginning November 12. The pre-load file will require up to 212 GB depending on your device, so make sure you've got ample space to begin pre-loading as soon as possible."

If you haven't bought GTA 6 yet but still want to preload it on Xbox Series X|S, you can do so by opening up the Xbox mobile app, going to the "Store" page (represented by a bag icon) and searching for Grand Theft Auto VI. You're specifically looking for "Grand Theft Auto VI" - not the Bundle version, but the standalone version.

In our case, it showed up as the fourth option down - you should see a variant of the following page when you open it:

Again, hitting the install button prior to 12am GMT on November 10th will install a small placeholder file, and then the full 200GB+ download will become available when the full game preload goes live.

That means everyone (except Xbox One owners, of course) has the ability to download GTA 6 on their Xbox consoles later today, so be sure to clear some room ahead of time - it's going to take up a heck of a lot of storage space!

Daniel Pemberton shares his reaction to watching an unfinished version of Beyond the Spider-Verse

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Spider-Man: Beyond the Spider-Verse has been a long time coming, but it sounds like it will be well worth the wait.

Composer Daniel Pemberton has shared his reaction to watching an unfinished version of the Marvel sequel, and it moved him to tears.

"The last cut I saw made me cry multiple times. And when something can do that when it's an animatic, and it's still early, it's like – I think everyone's going to be in for a real treat," Pemberton shared at Deadline Sound and Screen. "We all know we've got to make the greatest ending to a trilogy ever with that film."

Daniel Pemberton teases ‘Spider-Man: Beyond the Spider-Verse’ : “Everyone’s going to be in for a real treat” | #DeadlineSoundAndScreen https://t.co/mlOjXGV1TLNovember 7, 2026

The film was originally set to be released in 2024, but now won't arrive until 2027. That's a gap of four years since 2023's Beyond the Spider-Verse, which is especially agonizing since that movie ended on the huge cliffhanger of Miles Morales stranded in the wrong universe, facing down a Prowler version of himself.

"We put the most pressure on ourselves," producer Christopher Miller shared earlier this year. "There's no one that puts more pressure on us than ourselves, wanting to outdo ourselves each time and see things that you haven't seen before and make it feel like something you've never experienced before. And so, trying to get something that is as worthy as the previous two has been the driver."

The film arrives on June 18, 2027. While you wait, check out our guide to all the upcoming movies left of 2026 worth getting excited about.

#4032. The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel teaser all but confirms Hammerfell setting and means we can finally stop using that eight year old header image with the hills

Say hello to sandy scroll screengrab for the foreseeable future

Praise Talos and whatever other Elder Scrolls deities you might worship. We here at RPS and in the wider gaming press finally have new material to use when hunting for images to symbolise The Elder Scrolls 6. No more will we be limited to that shot of some hills from the 2018 teaser, because Bethesda have shown off an elder scroll covered in sand while revealing the new game's subtitle and all but locking in a setting. As a recent report from The Verge claimed, it's called The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel and looks to be set in Hammerfell.

These details were revealed in a short teaser at the end of a Todd Howard-fronted video celebrating Bethesda Game Studios' 40th anniversary. As such, the majority of the video is the Toddinator recapping the studio's history by touching on each of the games they've put out since 1986's Gridiron. Then, he looks to the future. "You know, everybody’s always asking about Elder Scrolls 6," the Toddfather said. "And we thought, hey, given the moment, what a perfect time to tell you what The Elder Scrolls 6 is actually called."

Cue a shot of an elder scroll buried in sand, followed by the The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel in fancy logo font. Then, a quote attributed to a moth priest called Yazar. "The scroll offered only a shimmer, a veil thinly lifted to my eyes. A future lost. A victory undone. Sands of time scattered by fate." OOH, CRYPTIC. In all seriousness, between the subtitle, the sand, and Yazar being referred to as a moth priest in service of High Queen Iradne of Hammerfell, the Verge report's assertion that the game will be set in Hammerfell is essentially set in stone by this teaser even if his Toddliness didn't spell it out himself.

Sentinel's the name of both a kingdom and city in the Redguards' province. The inclusion of an elder scroll in the teaser and the quote from Yazar also lend credence to the Verge report's claim that the game will make a big thing out of unravelling secrets linked to the provenance of these mysterious bits of paper. As for the quote's yammering of lost futures and undone victories, I'll venture to speculate that it could turn out to be reference to the player character thwarting a Thalmor victory, since Skyrim seemed to set up the elves as being on the verge of conquering Tamriel as the Cyrodillic empire fractured and fell.

That may or may not be the case, but we do know for sure that this teaser likely means a huge downturn in use of the header image below. It's eight years old, pulled from The Elder Scrolls 6's infamous 2018 teaser. All these years on, the game's finally on the way. You've served us well, screengrab of some hills. Talos guide you to wherever less regularly used images go.

Elder Scrolls teasing aside, it's worth bearing in mind that Bethesda parent company Microsoft have spent the majority of this year gutting their workforce with mass layoffs and studio ditching. Microsoft are also still currently subject to a BDS movement boycott over their reported ties to the Israeli military.

#4031. COD Modern Warfare 4's controversial Possum ability nerfed to stop it being used "as a combat mechanic instead of a survival mechanic"

Since the launch of Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's DMZ mode, players have been mainly arguing about two topics: whether there's a need for a PvE-only mode, and whether Possum - an in-game trait - has a place in an extraction experience.

And developer Infinity Ward has clearly taken a side in the Possum argument by implementing a key change to how it works. In Modern Warfare 4's latest patch, released overnight, the developer made it so that Possum - an ability that can revive a player - cannot be activated while the team that killed you is nearby. Possum also can't be activated if it's been less than four minutes since you were killed.

These two should address the most common complaints, but Infinity Ward left space for further tweaks in the future, such as by adjusting its range and duration.

If you're unfamiliar, Possum allows a player to revive themselves from a completely dead state once per match. To other players around, you appear to be dead and your body can be looted. But by using Possum, clever players were able to exact immediate revenge on their killers - or anyone else standing around near their apparent corpse - by springing back to life and shooting them in the back.

Possum's intended use was for dead players to have another shot at extracting from the match, rather than forfeiting the run entirely. Though their loot may be lost, Possum allowed players to save their operator.

Infinity Ward underlined this intention in a note accompanying the change. "The intention for Possum is to give a high level operator a second chance," the developer said in a blog post. "With the current iteration, Possum was being used as a combat mechanic instead of a survival mechanic.

"These tweaks are meant to prevent players from getting right back into the fight which they had just lost. We will be watching the use of Possum with this change to see if it has the desired effect."

Outside of that DMZ change, the 28th October patch includes a round of weapon balance changes. There are several buffs to assault rifles and SMGs, and some nerfs to the APOC-338 and FiNN LMGs. The buffs are notable given the across-the-board nerf Infinity Ward experimented with during the second beta weekend for Modern Warfare 4, which sought to increase the time-to-kill (TTK) impact of weapons, making them feel weaker as a result.

The patch also fixes several bugs players have been able to exploit in multiplayer and DMZ. And, in case you missed it, this is the patch that adds the Shipment map to the game - and yes, there's a 24/7 playlist.

Eurogamer's full review of Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 is due later today.

The game inexplicably became seven times larger on PC following an update

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

After a supposedly small update sent NieR: Automata's PC file size skyrocketing from a modest 50GB to over 366GB, the devs have finally been able to fix things so the action RPG won't eat up all your storage space.

The update in question arrived last week, and added Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, and Korean as extra languages. All valuable additions, of course, but unfortunately, things clearly didn't go quite to plan with the patch, with the game inexplicably becoming 600% bigger in the process.

While the official NieR account apologized and offered a temporary workaround, advising players to uninstall the game's DLC to slim things down to the intended size, the situation obviously wasn't ideal. However, things should now be back to normal for everyone. "We have identified the cause and now resolved this issue," a new post reads. "Apologies for any inconvenience caused."

We have identified the cause and now resolved this issue. Apologies for any inconvenience caused.November 9, 2026

For most people, this whole situation was probably more amusing than it was genuinely inconvenient, because, again, how does this even happen? To put it into perspective, the septupled file size made NieR: Automata over 72% larger than the 212GB pre-load size for GTA 6 on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S announced by Rockstar Games last week. Hell, it was even bigger than the monstrous 300GB that Phantom Blade Zero developer S-Game told players to reserve to pre-load its 145GB action RPG last month.

The NieR account's initial response to the situation was pretty funny, too, as it acknowledged that "installation requires significantly more storage space than intended." Yeah, just a bit.

For Nier Automata, Yoko Taro just made the RPG he wanted to and "tried to stay hidden from Square Enix as much as possible."

#4029. Sony Subsidiary Aniplex Ignores PS5 with Yet Another Game

Sony-owned publisher Aniplex will release dark fantasy visual novel LunaVerse on the Switch and PC next year, marking yet another occasion in which the subsidiary has skipped PS5.

The media firm, which is under the umbrella of Sony Music, has been releasing more titles of late – many of which don’t deploy on its parent company’s device.

Last year’s critically acclaimed The Hundred Line: Last Defense Academy is the most egregious recent example, attracting plaudits on the Switch and PC. Aniplex even purportedly helped fund the Too Kyo title.

I can certainly see why visual novels like LunaVerse aren’t necessarily the best fit for the PS5 – although I’d argue the popularity of the PS Portal has changed that paradigm somewhat.

Nevertheless, I still think it’s bizarre that a wholly owned Sony entity continues to release games not available on its parent company’s platform.

#4028. Mobile Suit Gundam Battle Operation 3 has been announced, marking another attempt at a free-to-play team game after Gundam Evolution's unfortunate fate

Bandai Namco have released the initial announcement trailer for Mobile Suit Gundam Battle Operation 3, a free-to-play team action game and a sequel to 2018's Battle Operation 2. The trailer is very, very pretty, showing off Gundam units clashing in large-scale battles and infantry fighting beneath the colossal mechas' feet (kinda like Titanfall, in having both human and mecha players in the same match). I'm sadly not yet enough of a true Gundam fan to recognise many of these units on sight other than the RX-78-2, but there's a real variety shown off here.

MOBILE SUIT GUNDAM GUNDAM BATTLE OPERATION 3　Announcement Trailer Watch on YouTube

While there's no release date specified in the trailer, Bandai Namco have confirmed that there will be a network test in Japan through November 20th-22nd, with an open network test planned for the future (thanks, Gematsu).

Following the fate of Gundam Evolution, a 2022 attempt at a hero shooter featuring Gundam units, it's nice to see another shot at taking the Gundam series into a team format. Evolution suffered from the all-too-common trappings of heavy microtransaction inclusion, with several playable Gundam units with unique abilities only available through paying real cash. It was rightly criticised for this, and since Bandai Namco seemed to have had high hopes for the revenue it could make from said microtransactions, the lack of money made meant it shut down just a year later.

Contrastingly, from what I can see, Gundam Battle Operation 2 was received fairly well on its release. While little is actually known about the third game at this point, let's hope it has a better chance than the series' last big release. I will quickly note that the trailer does close with a "*Some content may require purchase" note, so it'll likely have some form of microtransaction in itself — hopefully not to the same degree as Evolution. And, while we're on the topic of Gundam, there's also 2027's Gundam Rogue Orbit, a drastically different game that seems closer to a Devil May Cry-esque action title (though, unlike Battle Operation 3, will begin life as a timed exclusive to PS5). Now, if we could get a Gundam game that plays something like Armored Core, and god willing a proper PC release, I would be a very happy girl.

#4027. World of Warcraft players angry after Blizzard seems to contradict housing cosmetics policy with Halloween additions

The World of Warcraft team has found itself at the centre of controversy after recently-added housing cosmetics appeared to go against previous pledges not to sell decorations tied to the visual identity of the game's races and factions.

The cosmetics are the haunted Grimtide Estate and Grimtide decor packs - a spooky spin on Kul Tiran furniture that players can either buy through the Battle.net store or in-game shop. These decorations have a nautical theme, in line with the buildings present in the Battle For Azeroth expansion, where the Kul Tiran subfaction was added for Alliance players.

This has drawn the ire of World of Warcraft fans because it appears to go against a 2025 developer blog by Blizzard, which stated: "Housing items tied to core fantasies of a player's race or class, or that already exist in Azeroth, won't be sold in the shop. Thematically important decor that players know and love will also not appear in the shop."

Many of the housing items shown off in the Grimtide cosmetics appear to be visually tied to the Kul Tiran subrace, and some are almost identical to furniture seen in the Battle for Azeroth expansion. For example, a Grimtide dining chair with an anchor decoration carved into its back rest would not look out of place at all in a Kul Tiran house.

The counter-argument, however, is that these are differentiated enough by being Halloween themed. For example, the Grimtide Grand Piano has a big green tentacle slithering out of the instrument, which perhaps makes it spooky enough, and distinct enough, to be considered d separate from regular Kul Tiran furniture.

But even if you accept that argument, these decorations undeniably come close to the red line Blizzard itself established. And it is not the first time Blizzard has come under fire for its microtransactions.The Burning Crusade Classic Deluxe Edition included a special mount that was a point of controversy from players stalwartly against the inclusion of microtransactions in the game.

It caused so much dislike that players unhappy with its inclusion would use scripts to automatically spit-emote on those seen riding it, resulting in Blizzard disabling the emote shortly after.

The question now is whether Blizzard will see this upheaval as an opportunity to U-turn and reapproach premium housing cosmetics, or whether it will stay the course.

Meanwhile, World of Warcraft activity is poised to explode next week with the arrival of WoW Forever. This game, a new fork for the original MMO with new areas, raids, PvP maps and class changes, is set to release next month. Judging by the open beta, it's looking pretty good!

#4026. 'The Best RPG I've Played This Year' - Queen's Domain Is A Low-Key GOTY Contender On Xbox

Back at the end of last month, a little-known RPG launched on Xbox in the form of Queen's Domain, which we highlighted in our October 30th new releases roundup alongside 14 other titles that arrived that day.

Ever since then, we've been hearing various bits of praise for the game across multiple platforms, and it's gotten to the point where it's definitely a Game of the Year contender - albeit a very low-key one.

Officially, what you're getting here is a "retro-fantasy action RPG with brutal combat and traversal-focused exploration", and Queen's Domain is being compared to loads of legendary franchises including King's Field, Zelda and Dark Souls.

Here's what just a few people are saying about it on Steam, for example:

cautious asparagus on Steam: "It's the kind of game that keeps surprising you with the sheer scope and creativity. You know the first time in Elden Ring where you find the elevator that brings you down to Siofra River, and you're just in awe of how much more there is to the game? There are multiple times in Queen's Domain where you feel that same way. This is the best RPG I have played this year, and it might even be my game of the year."

Huell Babineaux: "Everyone says this is one of the best kings field successors out there and it probably is, but ive never played those games, so to me this game feels more like a dark and gritty first person legend of zelda, and it pulls this off exceptionally well. Combat is brutal and unforgiving, but also learnable. Exploration can be daunting and overwhelming, but always rewarding.

Powersteve on Steam: My game of the year. Not just the best King's Field imitator but a genuine improvement on the formula. Better combat, better variety of combat options and a massive world with some of the best level and secret design I have ever seen. Also remains engaging and balanced for the whole duration and doesn't turn into Doom with lightning bolts half way through like Lunacid. So good that I can't wait to get all the endings just so I can use those secrets to do a fresh run with sequence breaks which is something that I almost never do.

So, why haven't we mentioned this before? Well, the Xbox version of Queen's Domain was actually getting a bit of flack at launch, as people were pointing out a stuttering issue that seemed to be plaguing the Series X and S versions.

Looking at the reviews on the Xbox Store now though, the issue seems to have been addressed in a recent patch, and Queen's Domain is currently rocking a 4.7/5 rating on the US version of the Xbox Store as things stand.

In other words, this might well be worth picking up for your Xbox console! It's £16.74 / $19.99 if you fancy taking a punt in the near future, and we'll leave you with more details and screenshots for it down below.

Queen’s Domain is a retro-fantasy action RPG. Washed up on the shores of the Isle of Neasied, you set out to find your father and uncover the dark heart of this mysterious isle. Wield the Legendary Holy Sword Endu to take flight from platform to platform, and discover an interconnected, labyrinthine world where secrets and dangers lurk around every corner.

Fight action-oriented battles with a classic stamina meter, powerful charge attacks, weapon specific special attacks, and secondary throwing weapons. Level up, accessorize, and choose from a huge catalogue of melee weapons on your quest to fight your way through the hordes of monsters and powerful bosses awaiting you in the darkest depths of the isle.

If you pick up a DMZ bank vault keycard, you must first power the keycard reader and find a code

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

If you gain access to any of the MW4 DMZ bank vaults, you can pick up some serious cash alongside other valuable loot. Cash itself, though, is perhaps one of the most valuable resources you can exfil with thanks to DMZ's Vendor, who will sell you weapons and gear before your next mission - but they don't come cheap, making bank heists a worthwhile endeavor.

Pretty much everything you need for a bank heist can be found in or around the bank itself, but it's not entirely obvious what you need to actually do to get the vault open, so if you're looking to crank the vault door open for yourself, here's what you need to know.

There are four bank vaults in the MW4 DMZ map: One north of Songdo Wharf, another to the south of Wolves Stadium, one inside The Grid, and another in Cheongun Village.The three banks not located within The Grid are smaller bank branches and are much easier to loot as The Grid is an extreme-threat area. If you're heisting for the first time, I'd recommend starting with the eastern-most bank branch, to the north of Songdo Wharf.

To open DMZ bank vaults, you need three things: a car battery, a keycard, and a note showing most of the vault's unlock code. With these things in hand, follow these steps to unlock the vault:

Of course you'll be challenged during this process as your enemies will come after you, so take them out as and when they appear, particularly if you're tackling the main bank tower in The Grid. For that one, you'll definitely need to equip the best MW4 guns you've unlocked in the extraction mode, as well as a decent armor vest and at least one medkit.

As I've mentioned above, all of the required items can be found in or around the bank itself if you're lucky. Both the keycard and the code are always located within the bank, but a car battery can only be found in gas station stores, and you're not guaranteed to find one. While there is a gas station right next to the smaller bank branch, you're stuffed if there's no battery. There are three gas stations near the eastern branch, though, so your chances of finding a battery are much higher. You can also exfil with a battery, so look for one whenever you're near a gas station, then you can take it into a new match when you're thinking of robbing a bank.

For the keycard and code, simply look around the bank. The keycard is obvious, and the code is on a piece of paper. You'll only get the first three digits for the code, so you'll have to figure out the fourth via the process of elimination, but it's always the last digit.

#4024. Venom-toothed Noxious Terminids are soon to infest Helldivers 2, and it's your noble job to sterilise the galaxy for Super Earth

Helldivers 2 isn't slowing down any time soon, and according to Edwin's recent interview with Arrowhead CCO Johan Pilestedt, it'll continue to be Arrowhead's main priority for the future. As if Helldivers 2 wasn't full of enough horrors for our brave Super Earth Helldivers to shoot at for the betterment of galactic democracy, its next update is due to add an entirely new Terminid subspecies, the Noxious Terminids.

First up on are the Noxious Scavengers. These horrible little (see: huge) things skitter around at high speed and are loaded with deadly poison, but are thankfully at least fragile. Liberal use of area-of-effect weapons such as flamethrowers, explosives and flamethrowers are recommended to avoid being overrun by these horse-sized insects. Then there's the Noxious Spewer, which is not only fast like its smaller brethren despite its larger size, but also equipped with a web projectile which locks a Helldiver in place, vulnerable to a fatal bite. Oh, and if you dare shoot its soft underbelly, it violently explodes, with the same web fluid covering a wide area around it. The poison inflicted by these creatures' bites is a new damage over time effect that can blur vision, slow movement, eat away at your health, and make you fear this may be the end for you — so it's a bit like getting the flu (get your jabs!)

HELLDIVERS™ 2 | A Cleaner Galaxy Starts With You Watch on YouTube

This update also makes the change that bug caves can be found across many more worlds across the galaxy, leading troopers down tunnels with limited visibility and claustrophobic dead ends. Super Earth's propaganda, sorry, I mean, guidance, describes the galactic sterilisation program quite simply: locate the invasive species, identify the horrific monsters at the barrel of your flamethrower, and sterilise (burn to cinders). The guidance also, hilariously, includes the line: "Super Earth reminds you that ammunition is cheaper than antivenom." Now, get out there and rid our beautiful democracy of this vile pestilence.

#4023. "A cold dead place that's slowly decaying" - EA employees reveal a culture of secrecy and terrible morale following layoffs

Last week, EA announced it's laying off 400 workers across multiple studios, cancelling projects and refocusing on its biggest money-makers. As part of that, EA closed down the iconic BioWare studio, letting go of most of its remaining staff of around 50 people.

The mood inside EA is, unsurprisingly, low. Speaking to Vertical Slice, a number of current and former staff revealed a culture of secrecy surrounding layoffs, and a lack of clarity on who, exactly, is affected and how their teams are meant to move forward without them.

"My suspicion is that it is done to isolate the people laid off," one source said. "Depending on how large a layoff it is, it can take us a week or two or more to get our bearings back under us and figure out what we're doing."

This also affects the work itself, since in-progress projects become the responsibility of the fewer remaining members of the team. But a source revealed that it can take weeks for EA to communicate those specifics to staff and to chart a path forward.

EA's approach to telling affected employees they're being let go is one that should sound familiar to anyone who knows the modern corporate world. According to multiple sources, staff are invited to a Zoom call with chat disabled and the other participants hidden. They're then told they're being laid off, without being given the chance to ask any questions or say goodbye to their colleagues.

"You're getting laid off because you're just numbers on a list," one source said. " There's never an understanding of the actual project [you're working on]."

Sources also said EA is prioritising profits over the wellbeing of its people, now more than ever. As a result of EA's $55bn acquisition by a consortium of investors - chiefly Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund - EA is saddled with $20bn of debt it has to find ways to recoup.

"Morale has been terrible," another source said. "The line we kept hearing is 'do less, better' but it just felt like we were doing the same amount with less people. Upper management was very excited about Claude and the possibilities of [generative] AI, much to the chagrin of my team."

For the largest game publisher in the western world, all of this is unfortunate to see. But for many within EA, the decline has been seeping in for a while.

"That the recent email about the organisation changes [sounded like] it was written by a robot best sums up EA," one source said. "A cold dead place that's slowly decaying as leadership pilfers every last cent, leaving the rest of us to worry about how we feed our families."

Meanwhile, elsewhere in the games industry, the Xbox division is suffering through multiple waves of lay-offs, all with the cumulative aim of removing 3,200 people from their roles. Raj Patel, who's been tracking games industry layoffs, recently revealed on Bluesky that 2026 is on track to be the worst year on record in terms of the number of people laid off.

#4022. Free-to-Play Pirate Game Sea of Remnants Sails Closer with PS5 Closed Beta Next Month

Remember Sea of Remnants? Announced for PS5 last year during a summer State of Play, we've yet to see very much of the actual game so far, but it seems it won't be long before we can actually play it for ourselves.

That's because a closed beta test is scheduled for 3rd December 2026, and console platforms are being included for the first time. A select number of players will be able to check it out when it opens at 4pm PT on that date.

Yes, you can pre-register via the official website and be in with a chance of taking part in the test.

The news comes alongside a new cinematic trailer, which certainly has the visual flair present in the game's other showings so far.

Included in the closed beta will be a total of 21 playable characters.

"Players can experiment with different team compositions and turn-based combat strategies, from pursuit-focused combinations to area-of-effect (AoE) damage builds," reads a press release. "Character development and build customization offer further opportunities to refine tactics and tackle increasingly challenging encounters."

Participants will also have access to two regions, the White Sea and the Bridge Sea, upon which you can sail a pair of ship types.

I'll be honest, I've been very curious to play this since its announcement, as I still don't fully understand what the game even is. Fingers crossed I get into the beta, then.

We've talked quite a bit recently about the launch of World of Warcraft: Forever on PC and how it may end up being the biggest success of the year from an Xbox first-party perspective, and it seems that could actually be the case.

Its PC launch happened back on November 4th, and according to the folks at The Game Business, it's already broken multiple records for the series, including the biggest launch in WoW history based on peak concurrent players.

Here's a look at those records that have been broken:

Many people might overlook the success of WoW: Forever for Team Xbox simply because it's not shipping on consoles (at least not yet), but we reckon Xbox CEO Asha Sharma will extremely pleased by the game's success thus far!

It does seem to bode well for an Xbox Series X|S and/or Xbox Project Helix version in the future too - there's seemingly little point leaving money on the table when the new game is already optimised for controllers as it is.

Obviously it's still early days for WoW: Forever and the initial success will inevitibly drop off, but if they can retain enough interest in the months and years to come, Xbox will have an excellent new money spinner on their hands.

#4020. Frostpunk 2's The Surge DLC keeps the wintery apocalypse and adds in faction-clash-inducing electricity and sets a seasonally appropriate December release date

For the time being, the world of Frostpunk remains a hypothetical, even if it's one that seems just that little bit more likely than I'd like it to be given who's in charge of the world. But at the very least, there are pockets of hope to be found in Frostpunk 2, namely with its newly revealed next bit of DLC, The Surge, a name that has been bequeathed to it for incredibly obvious reasons. Oh, you need me to explain them? Fiiiiine.

You and your probably not so merry band of survivors have been trekking across the UK, when you end up at a "mysterious valley." Apparently some rumours have been going round about a "marvel left behind by history’s greatest mind - a relic with the potential to reshape the world itself." So you go off to look for it, and it essentially seems like this relic lets you use a whole bunch of electricity. Only, despite how useful this is for automating a bunch of work, various factions disagree over how it should be used, "while the secrets hidden within the valley prove far more difficult to uncover than anyone expected."

In terms of what you should expect from this DLC, for starters there's a new scenario to check out "set in an entirely new region, far beyond the borders explored in Frostpunk 2 so far." This relic is also implied to have come from the mind of one Nikola Tesla, you know, the electricity guy. There'll apparently be ways to utilise the Great Storm that's ruined the planet to "turn catastrophic whiteouts into valuable, harvested and stored resources." And you'll have some hidden treasures to find and mysterious to uncover in various nearby caves and ruins.

All sounds neat enough! And it's not too far away either. The Surge is currently slated for a seasonally appropriate December 14th release date. Let's hope no real world environmental disasters get in the way of that, 'ey? While you wait for it, you can wishlist the DLC on Steam.
